review: Dig good, dig better
nice

I fully completed the game, with unlocking all upgrades, including all parts for the car. I also nearly excavated out 2/3rds of the entire diggable area. (About down roughly to the satellite dish). 

First part of the game was enjoyable, but I was able to quickly get to the autodrill, which increased the overall quality of digging. Initially though, the stamina for the jetpack and the beer was incredibly frustrating since it felt like I couldn't go more than 20 seconds without needing to make my way back up. Eventually I was able to get the upgrades for no collision damage and unlimited digging stamina, so that increased the overall gameplay loop. 

The problem I mostly have is the "story"/receiver upgrades. I held off the final tier (Tier V) for a bit, as I wanted to try to excavate the entire area, but decided to check out what would otherwise occur-
[spolier]Spolier: If you made it down to the bunker, the final depth you can dig, then it just initiates an explosion, and you must make your way to the bunker, enter a code, and that's it.[/spoiler]

I felt like the ending was lackluster and outright pointless, since it dumped me right back into the main menu, presumably before my autosave or manual save, so I would have lost all progress up to that point, which felt lame. 
The final thing you get too, I am unsure if it does anything, or was just a joke, but it felt pointless into doing all that work, just for that. 

Additionally, the fall-damge/collision damage is outright dumb. I get that it's to prevent the player from outright just tunneling down or flying straight up, but with these types of games, it's to be expected, since otherwise how would you quickly get through it, so the amount of random objects buried that block your path, even after you've cleared the entire thing out, becomes incredibly annoying, since even with max jetpack upgrades (and no damage) it still takes multiple attempts to get out. 

The final thing I want to mention is the mutants/zombies: I like how they get harder each tier, but even with max upgrades, on everything, I started to take major damage in the final days, whereas before I was able to not even manually operate the turret, since they would all take care of the mutants. But in the final days, I while manually controlling the turret, still nearly had a few moments where I would have outright lost. The mutants feel a bit too OP, especially since even if you stay in the same tier, they just increase the amount everyday, presumably infinitely. 

Overall, I'd say the game is good, but the upgrades need a bit more balancing or they need more upgrades. I don't like having to choose between multiple things, especially like unlimited jetpack stamina or no fall damage, and the defenses need to be a bit more strong. 

(Also to everyone saying it's too grindy: I could have beat this game in half my hours, but since I wanted to clear out the entire thing, I took longer, intentionally going multiples of days without even upgrading. Just clear the cavern out, and get the vacuum upgrade, and it's super easy to rapidly get enough money. You don't even need the super nice stuff at the bottom, the cheap stuff adds up quick.)

The Spotter: Dig or Die è uno di quei giochi che magari prendi un po’ per curiosità… e poi ti ritrovi dopo ore ancora lì a scavare senza nemmeno accorgertene. Il loop di gameplay è semplice ma incredibilmente efficace: scavi, scopri, migliori e ricominci. Ed è proprio questa semplicità che lo rende così coinvolgente.

Il feeling generale è super rilassante ma allo stesso tempo stimolante, perché hai sempre qualcosa da fare o da ottimizzare. Ogni progresso ti dà quella soddisfazione che ti spinge a dire “ancora una run e poi smetto”… spoiler: non smetti.

Detto questo, il gioco ha anche dei limiti abbastanza evidenti. Dopo un po’, si sente la mancanza di contenuti: servirebbero più cose da sbloccare, più varietà e qualche meccanica nuova per mantenerlo fresco nel lungo periodo. È uno di quei titoli che ha un potenziale enorme, ma ha bisogno di parecchi aggiornamenti per esprimerlo davvero al massimo.

Nonostante questo, resta super divertente e perfetto se cerchi qualcosa di leggero ma che ti tenga incollato allo schermo senza stressarti.

The Spotter: Dig or Die, developed by Puppyroar Games and published by Forklift Interactive and Gamersky Games, is a hybrid survival experience that builds its identity around a clear and compelling contrast: quiet, methodical resource gathering during the day and chaotic, high-pressure defense at night. This dual structure defines the entire game, creating a loop that constantly shifts between planning and execution, and giving each in-game cycle a strong sense of purpose.

During daylight hours, the game leans into its mining and exploration mechanics. Players descend underground, carving through layers of terrain in search of resources needed to upgrade tools, repair structures, and expand their capabilities. This phase is deliberately paced, encouraging efficiency and careful decision-making as players weigh how deep to go and how much risk to take before nightfall. The digging itself feels responsive and rewarding, and as upgrades are unlocked, the process becomes faster and more satisfying. There is a steady sense of progression as basic tools evolve into more advanced equipment, reinforcing the idea that each expedition contributes directly to long-term survival.

When night arrives, the tone shifts dramatically. The calm of exploration is replaced by waves of hostile enemies attacking the player’s base, transforming the experience into a defensive challenge. Players must rely on the systems they have built—turrets, traps, and fortified structures—while also taking an active role in combat when necessary. These encounters test how effectively resources were gathered and used during the day, creating a direct link between preparation and survival. The tower defense mechanics are straightforward but effective, offering enough strategic depth to make each encounter feel engaging without overwhelming the player.

Progression is tied to a layered upgrade system that allows for different approaches to the game’s challenges. Players can prioritize improving their mining efficiency, strengthening their defenses, or enhancing their personal combat abilities. This flexibility encourages experimentation, as different strategies can lead to different outcomes depending on how resources are allocated. Artifacts and technological upgrades add further variety, giving each run a slightly different feel and helping to maintain engagement across multiple sessions.

One of the game’s strongest qualities is how seamlessly its systems are interconnected. The resources collected underground directly influence how well players can defend their base, and the success of those defenses determines how much progress can be made in subsequent cycles. This creates a loop that feels cohesive and rewarding, with each phase feeding naturally into the next. The balance between these elements is what makes the game particularly engaging, as players are constantly managing trade-offs between exploration, preparation, and survival.

Despite this strong foundation, the game does encounter some pacing issues. Resource management can occasionally feel restrictive, particularly when stamina or inventory limitations interrupt the flow of exploration. These interruptions can make certain segments feel more tedious than intended, especially during longer sessions. Additionally, while the upgrade system provides variety, not all upgrades feel equally impactful, which can reduce the sense of progression in later stages.

The overall structure is relatively concise, offering a complete experience within a moderate playtime. This works in the game’s favor by preventing it from becoming overly repetitive, but it also limits how much its systems can evolve over time. As players become more familiar with the loop, the experience can begin to feel predictable, with later stages relying more on increased difficulty than on new mechanics or ideas.

Visually, the game adopts a clean and functional style that prioritizes clarity, particularly during fast-paced nighttime encounters. The underground environments are easy to navigate, and the surface areas provide enough detail to support the game’s setting without distracting from gameplay. While the presentation does not stand out as particularly distinctive, it serves its purpose effectively, ensuring that players can focus on the mechanics without visual confusion.

Ultimately, The Spotter: Dig or Die succeeds by committing fully to its core concept and delivering a gameplay loop that is both structured and engaging. Its blend of mining, survival, and tower defense creates a satisfying rhythm that rewards planning and adaptability. While it may not offer extensive long-term depth and occasionally struggles with pacing, its focused design and interconnected systems make it a compelling experience for players who enjoy strategic resource management and defensive gameplay.

review:
Das Spiel wird Menschen gefallen, die repetitive Tätigkeiten und Dopamin-Fallen mögen.

Die Grundidee ist sehr stimmig. Es werden Genres verschweißt, was dann in Gestalt von Modi daher kommt und solche haben die meisten Spiele nicht, die ausschließlich eine Sache machen. Diese Modi, also Graben und Basis beschützen, synergieren wundervoll. Du investiert immer mehr in einen bestimmten Ort, demnach hast du Grund dort zu bleiben und ihn zu verteidigen. Nicht dass du Alternativen hättest, aber du verbringst da halt viel Zeit also wächst dir das ans Herz.

In der Zwischenzeit treibt der traditionelle ansteigende Loop alles voran. Ressourcen sammeln und in Upgrades stecken, die dich besser Ressourcen sammeln lassen plus andere perks. Deine Basis zu beschützen ist es was alles abrundet. Die Steigerung ist aber sehr langsam. 

Bei den Upgrades hätte man was deutlich besser machen können. Statt dass du alles über den Computer regelst und da was aus einem Menü auswählst, hättest du mit dem Schrott selbst zu den Geschützen gehen sollen. Es enttäuscht mich auch, dass man nicht mehr Dynamit tragen kann oder es verstärkt. Diese Verwaltungsebene ist uninspiriert und kann nur Gleichgültigkeit hervorbringen. Ach und man sollte diese Menüansicht mit nur einem Kopf schließen können statt dass man auf ein kleines Kreuz klicken muss.

Was ich bei der Erkundung des Erdreichs bemerkenswert finde, ist das Vorhandensein von markanten Punkten in der Erde, die unbeweglich und unzerstörbar sind. Es ist nämlich so, dass die Orientierung zunehmend schwerer wird ─ gerade weil du alles notgedrungen ständig veränderst. Außerdem dient das alles vermutlich als fail safe, damit der Spieler sich nicht in eine Sackgasse bringt, weil er alle Plattformen zerstört hat.

Was dieses Spiel hier tut ist möglicherweise nicht völlig originell. Mir fallen gleich mehrere verwandte Titel ein, die unter Umständen als Inspiration dienten. Der Look und der Ton hingegen geben dem hier seine Identität. Es ist cartoonhaft stilisiert und ulkig. Es ist als hättest du dein Haus auf einer Müllhalde gebaut. Die Amis machen sowas ja, ne? Ihren Müll vergraben? Die Dichte an Zeug, was du findest, ist absurd. Es ist besser man erwartet gar nicht erst irgendeinen abenteuerlichen Geist, was man ja generell annehmen könnte bei der Prämisse. Selbst ganz tief in der Erde sind noch Notizen und menschliche Anzeichen. Also Immersion und Atmosphäre waren keine Prioritäten.

Dass das schwer wegzulegen ist, liegt in der Natur seines Designs, jedoch sehe ich keinen Wiederholungswert, weil bei jedem Durchlauf alles gleich ablaufen wird.

[h1]The Spotter: Dig or Die — Le tower defense qui cache bien ses galeries[/h1]

Prenez le concept de [i]A Game About Digging a Hole[/i] — cette espèce de démo technique hypnotique où l'on creuse pour creuser — ajoutez un monde post-apocalyptique plein de secrets enfouis, une boucle jour/nuit entre exploration souterraine et tower defense, et vous obtenez un jeu au goût vraiment particulier. Ce mélange entre l'autisme de creuser à tout va et l'adrénaline de défendre sa base la nuit fonctionne bien, même s'il manque encore un peu de peaufinage.

[h3]Creuser, encore et encore[/h3]
La phase de minage est clairement le cœur du jeu. Il y a quelque chose de profondément satisfaisant dans le fait de descendre toujours plus loin, de découvrir ce que la prochaine couche cache. J'ai passé 12 heures d'addiction pure à essayer de creuser toute la map comme une gogol — et c'est le plus beau compliment que je puisse faire à un jeu de ce type.

[h3]Une alternance qui fonctionne... presque[/h3]
La boucle jour/nuit entre exploration et tower defense est bien pensée, mais accuse encore quelques faiblesses d'équilibrage. La difficulté des vagues est assez aléatoire : les mêmes défenses, les mêmes ennemis, et parfois ça passe tout seul, parfois ça vire à la catastrophe et votre intervention devient indispensable. Rien de frustrant ni de bloquant, mais on sent que ça mériterait encore un tour de vis.

[h3]Le shield de base et les artefacts : deux poids, deux mesures[/h3]
Deux éléments méritent d'être mentionnés. D'abord le shield sur la base — un bonus débloquable qui semble clairement indispensable, au point que jouer sans doit friser le supplice. Ensuite les artefacts roguelike... pourquoi ? Vraiment. C'est la grand-mère qui vous ressert une part de tarte alors que vous n'aviez clairement pas demandé. L'intention est bonne, mais ça s'intègre mal au reste et interroge sur sa raison d'être.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Une belle découverte qui, en creusant un peu, cache encore quelques faiblesses — mais aucune ne gâche le plaisir. Je recommande.[/b]

is an interesting twist on the tower defense genre. It has a simple story, sometimes even a rather silly one, and often tries to make you laugh with a kind of rough, deliberately dumb humor, including annoying sounds and moments that feel intentionally ridiculous.

What really sets it apart, though, is something else. The entire grinding loop is not really based on the rewards you get from surviving enemy waves, but almost entirely on digging through a massive pit full of trash to gather resources. It is a pretty unusual idea, and it does give the game a distinct identity compared to other titles in the genre.

The two main flaws, at least for me, are fairly clear. The first is the sharp increase in difficulty with each new wave, which pushes you to try to finish the game as quickly as possible instead of actually enjoying the progression. The second is that, after a while, even the digging starts to lose its charm. After a few hours of digging and shooting, the game begins to feel repetitive, even if you can still sense some progression in certain parts of the gameplay.

In the end, it is a game that manages to be enjoyable thanks to its core idea, but it also loses a good part of its originality after just a few hours.

Did you play A Game About Digging A Hole and wish there was, well, more of it? Then you'll probably have a lot of fun with The Spotter. 90% of the gameplay revolves around digging a hole in a small patch of land outside your post-apocalyptic gas station to find scrap - you spend scrap to upgrade your digging tools and personal stats so that you may dig bigger holes, and so on. The "twist" is that every night a horde of mutants will attack your gas station, so you need to climb up top and use the turret on top to blow them up before they can break in and kill you. You can spend scrap on that, too, by the way.

The turret defence gameplay is about 2 mins for every 20 mins or so of gameplay, so most of your time will be spent digging. And.. the digging mechanics are pretty good! Your stamina and your backpack start annoyingly low, but that's kind of the point - you're incentivised to upgrade them and after a while that won't be an issue anymore. You'll occasionally stumble on little puzzles hidden in the dirt, and they're pretty fun to get around.

The game is made using that one post-apocalypse asset pack that everyone uses - you know, the one that also has a medieval asset pack that everyone also uses. Having said that, it uses it pretty well, even if the player model is completely out of style with it. Its honestly pretty fun! The game will ask if you're okay with "Toilet Humour" - what it means by that is if you're okay with your character randomly farting every now and then.

My only real complaint was that despite it being a whole collectable hunt, the car you can repair is.. thoroughly underwhelming. You can use it to drive around running over mutants at night, but other than the novelty of doing that its not a particularly useful strategy. Which is a shame!

Took me about 10 hours of not particularly focused gameplay to get the ending, and a large amount of that was spent excavating a few of the big objects you can find underground. I had more than 12 euroes worth of fun, so honestly, if this game interests you go for it.

В целом, игра неплохая. Любителям копалок, или клинеров должна зайти. Что касается TDшной составляющей (обороны от зомби) то какой-то интерес разве что пару волн, при переходе на новый уровень развития (маяка), когда появляются новые монстрики, а вы ещё не закупились новым оборудованием.
Игра ОООООчень репитативная, вы будете нырять в яму и вылезать обратно 100ни, а то и 1000чи раз, периодически отвлекаясь на расстрел мутантов.
Прокачка есть, и она чувствуется, что в обороне, что в копании, вот только она чувствуется скорее потому что всё очень урезано в начале. В начале вы стреляете пару раз и перезаряжаетесь пол часа, чтобы стрельнуть ещё пару раз, а урон никакой. Копаете вообще чайной ложкой а не лопатой, а энергии хватает на пару капков. Если бы в начале было то что в конце, а под конец вообще какой-то супер-пепер-гипер шмот, было бы лучше.
Строить вы будете - , а не будете... есть заранее прописанные места для всех турелек (которые кстати, мало эффективны до самого конца) и ловушек\заборов. Единственное, вам всё же дадут некие выборы в ветке прокачки, в какую сторону двигаться (например, снайперская турель, пулемётная или миномётная), что правда отбросит другие варианты, и вам придётся переигрывать всю игру заново ради ачивок.
Что касается копаний, то копать в будете не как угодно, а в заранее созданной трубе, засыпанной грунтом и ресурсами. В трубе так же есть некие особые места, аля провалившаяся машина, автобус, катер, комнаты, пещерка и т.п. но всё же сама "Шахта" это почти ровный цилиндр, что не даёт особых вариантов для копаний в стороны, или пластами или ешё как. К тому же, в игре не хватает каких-то лесенок, дополнительных шоткатов или сборщиков ресурсов. Вы будете спускаться всё глубже, а потом со всё большей глубины таскать всё на поверхность. (в игре есть артефакт, который сделает ещё одну сосалку ресурсов, но это не то).

Если не париться ачивками, и сразу прокапаться в глубь, то игру можно пройти за несколько часов, где основное время уйдёт на разблокировку уровней передатчика (прогресс прокачки). Ну а выкапывать всё и вся, тут можно десятки часов.

То что есть, хорошо, но как буд-то нужно больше. В целом, советую попробовать.

[h1]越挖越上头，越守越着急[/h1]
游戏名字起的让我以为制作组要考公，游戏名字基本体现了游戏的内容，它把“挖矿”“守家”“资源经营”这几件事硬是拧成了一个很紧张的循环。刚开始我还以为它只是那种偏轻松的“收破烂”探索游戏，顶多晚上再来点防守元素平衡一下，结果真正玩下来才发现，这游戏根本不是让你悠闲挖宝的，它更像是在逼着你一边抢资源、一边赶进度、一边防止自己被夜里的怪潮狠狠干碎。也正因为这样，它玩起来会有一种很特别的上头感，白天在地下越挖越深，捡到值钱玩意儿的时候会兴奋，回到地面把材料砸进升级树的时候也很爽，但爽完立刻又得开始担心今晚顶不顶得住。

游戏的玩法循环其实做得挺扎实，白天下地底刨垃圾、金块、钻石和各种奇奇怪怪的隐藏点，晚上回地面守住据点，撑过去以后继续把资源投进钻头、背包、炮台和基地防御。这个循环本身是很容易让人沉进去的，因为每一次外出都不只是为了“多挖一点”，而是在给下一晚换取更安全的包围措施。你会很自然地进入那种“再来一趟”“再多带一点上去”“这波资源换完应该能轻松一点吧”的状态。再加上游戏还塞了不少风格很怪但挺令人印象深刻的小东西，比如突然冒出来的 UFO、一些地下奇景、黑色幽默味很重的设定，整体气质不是那种特别正经的末世求生，反而有点又荒诞又恶趣味的 B 级片味道，这点还挺让人喜欢的。

但问题也很明显，而且基本都集中在“过渡碎片化的游玩体验”这件事上。游戏想营造忙碌感，这没错，可它现在很多游戏机制叠在一起以后，不是紧凑，而是烦。最直观的就是背包容量、体力限制、返程手段这几个系统一起发力，导致你经常不是在探索，而是在来回跑流程。正挖着爽呢，包满了；想再多挖一会儿，体力又见底；准备回去，喷气背包又给你一种不上不下的无力感。更别说有时候白天还会被奇怪事件打断，比如飞碟来偷狗，这种设计第一次见会觉得有点搞笑，多来几次就会开始烦，因为它本质上还是在强行打断你的采集节奏。

另外，游戏的成长反馈来得有点慢，按理说这种挖矿建造类游戏，最重要的就是“越玩越顺手，越玩越爽”的快感，要让玩家明显感觉到自己从小铲子小背包的可怜虫，慢慢进化成高效率的“垃圾挖掘机器”。但这作目前在这方面的游戏设计体验仍有待优化，很多升级提升是有，但体感没有想象中那么明显，尤其前中期会比较折磨。你明明花了资源，结果挖掘效率、返程体验或者防守压力并没有立刻改善多少，爽点很难立马感知到。炮台系统也是类似问题，看上去是基地防御的核心，实际上前期更像是辅助，你还是得自己频繁补枪救火，AI 也不算聪明，很多时候不是你在享受塔防，而是你在替AI擦屁股。

还有一点会很影响心情，就是失败惩罚偏重，基地一旦被推掉，重来的代价不小，但游戏又没有特别成熟的永久成长体系去缓和这种挫败感。换句话说，它不是那种“这局死了没关系，下局会更强”的设计，而更像“你得慢慢重新来过”。这种“传统”的做法不是不行，可前提是手感和流程得足够顺，不然玩家更容易感受到的不是挑战，而是疲惫。再加上目前还有一些BUG和小毛病，会进一步放大这种挫败感。

总体上讲，这款游戏不是没想法，恰恰相反，它的想法挺多，而且核心框架其实挺有吸引力。问题在于它现在还没有把这些想法真正优化好。它有让人熬夜再来一局的潜质，也确实做出了那种“白天挖到停不下来，晚上守得手忙脚乱”的独特节奏，但同时它又经常因为过多的限制、反复折返和不够干脆的成长反馈，把这种上头感拽回到疲劳感里。在当下我会把它看成一款创意很足、完成度还差些许的作品。喜欢挖“垃圾”、塔防、资源管理，而且能接受一点“地狱笑话，黑色幽默”的玩家，大概率能从里面找到乐子；但如果你更在意游玩流畅度、爽感释放和长线成长，那这游戏目前可能还得再等等。

They tried to make a FPS version of Dome Keeper but, in my opinion, ended up with a boring game with none of the fun, replayabilty or challenge of Dome Keeper. After 14hrs I had to stop.

The game is a repetitive mess.

1. There is no strategy since, if you pace yourself when uptiering, you can just hoard resources while the mutant hoards stay at the same difficulty. Hence no pressure to try a different approach.
2. A lot of special items you find are pointless (temporary infinite jet pack, full stamina) considering you will run into full backpack/no stamina anyway thus forcing you to surface. There are way too many pointless collectables (hula dolls, cheese, stuffed toys) to allow me to take this game seriously.
3. Absolutely pointless and cringeworhy ability to piss with the right mouse button. Now making me take the game even less seriously.
4. Every third night or so there is a storm instead of mutants, making it a bit darker - absolutely pointless since you have light sources. It is also brings the game away from being about the gameplay challenge of digging, finding, defending which Dome Keeper did so well (and which is obviously the core idea which they copied).
5. The final straw for me was finding a room buried deep down (no idea how far through the game this point is), where it turns into a badly done platformer with moving lasers and where your jetpack is deactivated just so you have to do it. The game definitely does not shine when it comes to movement/world design/fall damage and at the last jump I failed and got lasered to death. Not fun. It didn't even make sense that I didn't actually die and instead was just transported to the surface.

Just a mess, which I grew tired of. Maybe others will find all the "quirkiness" funny or endearing (that's great if you do) but for me it demonstrated more evidence that the art of game developing evades most developers.
Banger!

Если вам нравится копать глубоко, строить умно и стрелять метко — The Spotter станет вашей новой зависимостью. Это маленькое инди-чудо, которое доказывает: даже на заброшенной заправке можно построить нечто великое.

It has a childish charm. I'm easily drawn in by diggy hole escapism.

It's quite competently made, it has a nice detailed world, a questionable but sometimes funny sense of humour, but by the end this one leaves a particularly pointless aftertaste. 

You have no real meaningful control over the upgrades to your camp - the order in which you buy things doesn't matter, the defenses are ineffective and feel undercooked. There are a lot of options and small details in this game that feel like they're there for no reason, making little to no difference to gameplay, just filling up the tech tree without any real function.

The dig site being a narrow vertical shaft with a *lot* of unbreakable walls/floors/ceilings really crushes any sense of exploration or agency. There are no meaningful choices, ever.

 It's very grindy past a certain point, but without the surprises or evolutions in gameplay that can sometimes justify grind. It felt like it didn't know how to end, and the digging and travelling merely became more and more time-consuming and dull by the finals depths of the dig site before a disappointingly bland conclusion.

Ultimately The Spotter is 90% filler, despite a promising start, and feels like it lacks an identity. It has more visual charm and humour than many other incremental or digging games but it's only a colourful skin over a shallow experience. I'll withhold additional puns about a lack of depth.

Maybe a future game from this developer could attempt a more expansive world, more significant upgrade variety, more interesting combat, more player-choices and opportunities to weigh risks and decisions in where you invest your time and equipment?

Thumb Sideways (Recommended only for Alcoholics and Masochists)

The "Drunk Digger" Simulator

Let’s get one thing straight: I didn’t know I was buying a simulator for a functional alcoholic. My character has the physical endurance of a wet paper towel.

The Stamina "Logic": You dig for 30 seconds? Congratulations, you’re now clinically exhausted and need... a beer? Seriously? Every time I move a pebble, my guy starts gasping like he’s run a marathon, and the only "cure" is to haul ass back to the surface to chug more brew. Is this a game about finding loot, or a government funded campaign to promote alcoholism? Give me a break and let me dig the damn ground without needing a pub break every two minutes. Fix the damn stamina!

The Inventory & Junk: The drop rate for absolute garbage is astronomical. I dig a little bit and suddenly I’m buried in literal wagons of ♥♥♥♥. Meanwhile, my backpack clearly isn’t made of rubber. I spend more time managing trash than actually playing.

The Good Stuff (Why I haven't refunded).

Performance: Surprisingly smooth. It actually runs without melting my PC.
The music is genuinely decent.
 Bunker 1  music. If it wasn’t for those godforsaken zombies, I’d probably just move in there and ignore the surface entirely.

If you enjoy being a thirsty digger who can't carry anything and has a serious drinking problem, this is 10/10. For everyone else, wait until the devs realize that humans can actually breathe and work for more than 30 seconds without a cold one.

review:
[h1][b]The Spotter: Dig or Die - L'addiction pure du minage et de la survie (6.5/10)[/b][/h1]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hzBNEgLHX8M

[h2][b]Introduction - Une pelle, un sac et des zombies[/b][/h2]

[b]The Spotter: Dig or Die[/b] est un titre qui comprend parfaitement ce qui rend un jeu indépendant addictif : une boucle de progression gratifiante. Vous gérez une station-service isolée dans un monde dévasté. Le concept est simple mais redoutable : vous devez creuser pour survivre. Mais attention, ici la pelle n'est pas seulement un outil, c'est votre assurance vie face aux hordes de zombies qui n'attendent que le coucher du soleil pour vous dévorer.

[h2]🕹️ Le Cycle de Jour : Minage et Recyclage[/h2]

La journée est consacrée à l'exploration et à la préparation. C'est la phase "calme" mais tendue du jeu :
[list]
[] [b]Forage Tactique :[/b] Vous descendez sous votre base pour dénicher des métaux rares. Chaque coup de pelle compte. La sensation de découvrir un nouveau gisement est extrêmement satisfaisante.
[] [b]Le Système de Recyclage :[/b] Une fois vos métaux collectés, vous devez les passer au recycleur de la station. Rien n'est jeté. Ces matériaux sont la monnaie d'échange pour tout votre équipement.
[*] [b]Améliorations Vitales :[/b] C'est ici que le jeu devient accrocheur. Vous devez améliorer votre [b]pelle[/b] pour percer des roches plus dures et votre [b]sac à dos[/b] pour transporter plus de ressources. On se surprend à calculer chaque trajet pour optimiser ses récoltes avant la tombée de la nuit.
[/list]

[h2]🛡️ Le Cycle de Nuit : Défense de Base[/h2]

Quand le soleil disparaît, le jeu change radicalement de visage :
[list]
[] [b]Siège Zombie :[/b] Les zombies attaquent votre station. Vos ressources recyclées servent alors à fortifier vos murs et à alimenter vos systèmes de défense.
[] [b]Tension Maximum :[/b] Tout ce que vous avez amélioré durant la journée (vos gadgets, vos protections) est mis à l'épreuve. Si votre base tombe, c'est la fin.
[/list]

[h2]🎨 Ambiance et Technique[/h2]

[list]
[] [b]Esthétique Post-Apo :[/b] Le jeu offre un style visuel "Dieselpunk" très réussi, avec des effets de lumière superbes lors des phases souterraines.
[] [b]Interface Intuitive :[/b] La gestion de l'inventaire et du sac à dos est claire, ce qui est crucial quand on doit vider ses poches en urgence.
[*] [b]Sound Design :[/b] Le bruit métallique de la pelle et les cris lointains des zombies créent une ambiance lourde et immersive.
[/list]

[h2]✅ Points Positifs[/h2]

[list]
[] [b]Boucle de gameplay parfaite :[/b] Le mélange minage/recyclage/défense fonctionne à merveille.
[] [b]Progression constante :[/b] On sent réellement la différence à chaque amélioration du sac à dos ou de la pelle.
[] [b]Satisfaction du recyclage :[/b] Transformer des vieux métaux en ressources de pointe est très gratifiant.
[] [b]Challenge équilibré :[/b] Le jeu vous pousse à aller toujours plus profond malgré le danger.
[/list]

[h2]❌ Points Négatifs[/h2]

[list]
[] [b]Début de partie un peu lent :[/b] On se sent très limité par le petit sac à dos au tout début.
[] [b]Gestion de la faim/soif :[/b] Les allers-retours au frigo peuvent parfois couper l'élan de l'exploration souterraine.
[/list]

[h2]🎯 Verdict[/h2]

[spoiler]The Spotter: Dig or Die est une pépite pour les joueurs qui aiment la progression "step-by-step". Le lien entre l'extraction minière et la survie nocturne est organique : on ne creuse pas juste pour le plaisir, on creuse pour avoir le métal qui permettra de forger la tourelle qui nous sauvera la vie. C'est addictif, bien pensé et visuellement très propre.

[b]Verdict :[/b] Un hybride minage/survie indispensable pour les amateurs de craft et de Tower Defense.
[/spoiler]

[i]Statut : Disponible sur Steam - Développeur : Puppyroar Games[/i]
Sure, it's repetitive, but that's kinda what you're getting into buying most digging games.

[h1]简介[/h1]
营地的最深处究竟埋着什么秘密？为什么外星人总想劫持我的狗？白天并不能悠闲的渡过，要争分夺秒的多回收一些材料，不然晚上的战斗压力会很大，这样的日子，什么时候才是头。《丧尸末世：地底全是财，挖宝造炮台》是一款末世生存加塔防防守的游戏。玩家将操作一个末世的幸存者，在自己的营地里挖掘、建造、防守外星人或者是晚上的袭来的变异者。
[h1]角色和营地的成长[/h1]
游戏开始会在一个简陋的营地，设施不全，防御性也不高。玩家操作着主角，在这个末世开始艰难的求生，首先是不断的挖掘营地收集那些可回收的垃圾换成可用的金属材料，渴了就到冰箱找点的啤酒美美的来上一口。主角装垃圾的背包上限，但可以通过天赋不断扩容背包，也可以强化挖掘手段，还可以在探测器的帮助下，可以挖到值钱的宝藏。材料多了就能去加强营地的反击和防御能力。
[h1]防守玩法[/h1]
晚上如果天气不好，就不会有怪物攻击，可以幸苦点但能安稳的渡过一天，如果天气正常就会有变异者进攻营，变异者开始进攻会有明显的提示和要击杀变异者数量的要求，这个时候就要快点跑到楼顶炮台的位置操作炮台。战斗的玩法也很简单，跟抢滩登陆差不多，环360°旋转找到变异者并进行击杀，变异者击杀达标了晚上的防守就算结束了，可以去睡觉了。营地的升级还可以选择增加辅助机枪，会自动攻击，升级一下可以提高攻击效率，在升级一下营地的防御，防守上基本就没啥压力了。天赋升级还有个喷气背包，这个也很重要，营地挖的太深了可能跳不出来了，有喷气背包就没这个问题了，但要注意喷气背包的能量。
[h1]彩蛋[/h1]
游戏中也有一些好玩的彩蛋，比如挖地没多久就可以挖到一个避难所，只是里面没有幸存者了，只有不用吃喝的机器人还在，周围摆放了很多娃娃。还可以在庇护所里拿到一个被动能力，中期的车棚钥匙也是在这里拿。还有个彩蛋就是白天会有外星人开着宇宙飞船来偷狗！如果狗子被偷走了过一段事件，狗会头戴一个控制器逃回来，这个时候狗就会控制小型的宇宙飞船帮助主角在晚上进行防守。
[h1]总结[/h1]
总的来说，这是一款量大管饱的游戏，挖掘、建造、塔防，还有资源管理。虽然玩到后期天赋看板基本都能点满，但过程还是挺有意思的。每个阶段的提升都能给主角带来实质性的变化，开始是用铲子，然后是钻头，每次提升都是肉眼可见的变化，当然也很期待这个游戏中的科技风格，不断驱动主角往下挖看看究竟有什么，但天然气爆炸是什么鬼，emm，多少是带点恶趣味。

[h1]⛏️ The Spotter: Dig or Die — decent idea, weak execution[/h1]

[b]🎮 I run the curator group [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45719096/]Build, Rule, Repeat[/url] — simulators and system-driven games where mechanics matter.[/b]

[hr]

[h2]🌍 Digging with potential[/h2]

The Spotter: Dig or Die builds its core around digging, exploration, and terrain interaction.  
At first, it feels like there’s something interesting here — a system that could evolve into a satisfying gameplay loop.

But the deeper you go, the more the cracks start to show.

[hr]

[h3]🧠 What works:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Decent core idea around digging and exploration  
[*]Simple and easy-to-understand mechanics  
[*]Short sessions can be mildly enjoyable  
[/list]

[hr]

[h3]⚠️ What breaks it:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Top-tier shovel feels underwhelming  
[*]Progression lacks impact  
[*]Ending feels unsatisfying and abrupt  
[*]Terrain physics feel extremely weak  
[*]Digging never becomes truly satisfying  
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]⚙️ Gameplay & Feel[/h2]

The biggest issue is the core mechanic itself — digging.  
It should feel powerful and rewarding, especially with upgrades.

Instead, even with the best tools, it feels slow, weak, and lacking feedback.

And the terrain physics don’t help.  
The ground doesn’t behave in a convincing or interesting way, which removes a lot of potential depth from the entire experience.

[hr]

[h2]🏁 Final Verdict[/h2]

The Spotter: Dig or Die has a solid idea at its core, but struggles in execution.  
When your main mechanic feels unsatisfying, everything built on top of it suffers.

[b]Not terrible, but disappointing — especially by the end.[/b]

The Spotter: Dig or Die is a fresh and engaging indie survival game that perfectly blends digging mechanics with tense tower‑defense action. I really enjoyed the “dig by day, defend by night” concept—it feels unique and keeps the gameplay varied and exciting. The post‑apocalyptic setting is atmospheric, and the low‑poly art style gives the game a stylish, modern look that works really well.

What impressed me most is how everything is connected: every resource you dig up, every hole you carve, and every barricade you build directly affects your chances of surviving the nightly mutant waves. The progression feels rewarding, and the moment you finally restore the main receiver and catch that last message is incredibly satisfying. Overall, The Spotter: Dig or Die is a polished, addictive experience that I would definitely recommend to fans of survival and tower‑defense games

review: Relaxing and entertaining

So I just finished this one!
And I have to admit this game was really deep!

Although only about 100m or so? Which translates into a playtime of roughly 6 hours depending on your effectiveness. Since it is in essence a resourcecollection game you will spend a lot of time digging up these resources and convert them into cash to use for upgrades. Spotter deviates from the usual bunch and adds three different types of currency (iron, gold and diamond) which are depending on your layer found in different quantities and qualities. As per usual your hard earned money will be spend on your tools making the dig easier and faster BUT this time you also have to invest cash into upgrading your base and you main turret. 
Once nighttime comes the mutants are trying to attack your base. So besides digging you have some light tower defence baked in as well adding a bit more action. 

There is a story yes but this only resolves around upgrading a key structure a couple of times to trigger the final dig down. At least to keep your sense of discovery entertained you will find special areas that either unlock new mechanics (like the car seen in the trailer) or give you an instant upgrade that is not available in the normal upgrade tree. 

Overall I was decently entertained and if you are not careful you might even finish the whole game in one sitting. As usual... these kind of games once they got you in their grasp can bury you
6.5/10 and the undiscounted price is more than acceptable

世界破破烂烂，我在捡捡破烂。
这个世界很危险，也很孤独，咱独自守着基地，一边挖挖挖，一边突突突。
白天当矿工，晚上打丧尸，偶尔还会有外星人来凑个热闹，这个世界可真是有点操蛋哦。
矿工怎么当，沿着土坑一路往下挖就好了。
路上的垃圾都捡起来回收，获得铁、金和钻石等资源。
资源用来升级科技树，升级角色、炮塔和基地各种科技。
当然，地下也不一定只有来及，还有神器、收藏品、特殊物品甚至是一些活人以及特殊场景等内容，所以地下一切皆有可能。
至于面对夜晚的尸潮来袭，其一是主角在塔顶拿着狙击枪（炮）对着丧尸突突突，其二是科技树解锁基地活力炮塔自动攻击。
玩家突突突的设计手感还不错，尤其是爆头击杀丧尸的那一下，音效、特效都贼带感。
游戏玩着有亿点点上头，一直挖挖挖，就有种停不下来的魅力，好嗨皮哦。
不过，面对披萨（共有10个）、硬币（共有20个）、毛绒玩具（共有5个）、异域舞者（共有10个）、奶酪（共有10个）等收藏品，寻找到全部还是好难。
另外，诸如钥匙、汽车零件有些特殊物品，寻找起来也很是不容易。
不过，这些也是游戏中有趣的一环，还是不错的。

review: Started playing this game like pressure washer cleaner, just cleaning all the dirt away, very satisfying and chill.

[h1]末日来袭，我竟成为最强幸存者！——《丧尸末世：地底全是财，挖宝造炮台》[/h1]   
丧尸末世降临，海量变异体席卷荒野。一觉醒来，他们来了！只剩我和这座快要报废的加油站。我能否绝地求生？且看我大杀四方！

[h2]什么？开局只有一把铲子？[/h2]   
作为最强幸存者，我的状态肯定是各种buff拉满，数不尽的物资加上超级武器系统，什么小小丧尸，那不是手到擒来。
现在，你告诉我，我只有一把铲子和一冰箱啤酒？？？左上角的消息告诉我，让我先捡5个垃圾。
于是，在小小的土地里面挖呀挖呀挖，挖一个罐头，再挖个扳手。不一会，背包已满，及时出售给旁边的回收机，你将会获得一个零件。
可以说，零件的作用非常大，在天赋解锁及接收器升级方面，有着巨大的作用！
挖着挖着没劲了怎么办，别着急，去冰箱来瓶冰啤酒，一下子活力满满。

[h2]夜晚来袭，我化身成最强兵王[/h2]    
深夜来袭，四面八方的丧尸扑面而来，今晚，我将是最强兵王，作为cs超级玩家，这种小小的射击简直是轻松easy，枪枪爆头，一个字，“爽！”
不过，过程中，仍有两个小问题，一是如果你不打头，打身子就得两枪。二是右下角有个弹夹，打完换弹时间超级长，还有个冷却系统，意味着玩家只能单点，不能连击。在后期僵尸多的条件下，一定要做好这方面的规划。

[h2]最强神器+天赋系统，我已无敌！[/h2]    
就拿天赋系统来说，共分为三大类。角色、炮台、基地。
角色方面，就是有铲子大小——决定是否挖的更快。
背包管理——提升容量。还有打火机之类的。
而炮台方面，ai瞄准，扩容弹夹、伤害修正等等，让玩家打个痛快。
最后的基地方面，各种辅助升级，主要以服务炮台为主。
当玩家收集好相关物资后，解锁相关天赋，就能变得更强，这里建议先升级角色，后期在补充其他板块。
而神器系统，就更牛逼了，这个是我在挖掘到地堡时发现的，可以看到，每个属性都很强，最后我选择了乌龟壳，更加稳妥。

[h2]一点感悟[/h2]    
《丧尸末世：地底全是财，挖宝造炮台》玩起来，给我最大的感受是轻松，其实游戏得到核心就是收集资源+建造生存。
但是在收集资源过程中，其实给了玩家很大的余地，自由挖掘以及突然出来的神奇物品，让游戏变得充满惊喜。
如果你也是卡通风格的收集+战斗类爱好者，强烈推荐一试！

友情提示：每晚过后，记得维修基地，要不开局半血，打得会很吃力。

太变态了这个游戏，玩了十几年仅有的一款玩两三个小时就会晕的游戏，忍者组的炫光都没破我防，全低关运动模糊，500多帧，low帧几乎没有，就是头晕恶心想吐，demo都没这种情况。
    而且一挖到砂土层经常卡模型，视野穿透，模型缓加载，散热水冷都压不住，老子上层土都给你清光了，还他妈吃算力。本来想挖都快挖完了，每两小时休息休息，忍忍得了，结果想保存，一不小心错点了菜单栏的加载，一想到又要再清一次土。

    破防了，直接放过自己，太折磨了。如果你本来就晕3D，听我一句劝，别买，别玩。你吴京，你血性方刚，电你两下你啊啊啊啊啊叫几声就过去了，这破游戏让你玩还没问呢淌着口水几把什么都招了，精神酷刑。正常人我也建议不如拿这钱去麦当劳买个双层吉士汉堡。这福游戏数值卡的要死，升满了也没强到哪去，龟儿的图又大，一样牙签搅大缸。打僵尸也没意思，一不割草二没操作，最高难度定位准也就那样，但不管它这破自动你基地又稳定炸，新鲜感一过去烦不胜烦。还有这挖宝，我不知道怎么评，但是给我就是一种感觉，麻木，完全感受不到挖到高价值的快乐。铁，金，钻，三个价值的货币卡的死死的，一共四层挖到第三层才有转换神器。升级要指定货币，没拿之前你没挖到就是没挖到，挖再高价值的下级货币垃圾也没用（而且垃圾很多，完全就是堆量，而不是靠吃低保然后一波暴富）。等你拿到了，转化比1000：50：1根本换不动，升级也要大量下级货币，想提升不如sl花钱去抽老虎机。我其实很想慢慢挖不借助老虎机，但是身体实在扛不住。挖砂土层一半就升满了，代价就是奔头也没了，下一层淤泥层真就没动力了，就是机械的挖。

A fun little game

If you are looking to spend around 5 to 10 hours on a relaxing digging/towerdefence/fartjokes game, then this is the game for you.

The digging is addictive but there were things that I found really annoying, and it only partially got better:
1. Endurance mechanic (my main gripe)- Throughout the game you will have to constantly run back to the refrigerator to get a drink to replenish your endurance to continue digging. Your endurance only looks to regenerate up to maybe 5% of what your total endurance is, which is useless. There doesn't appear to be any upgrade, or any way to bring some drinks with you while you dig. You will find some refrigerators deeper down, somewhere near the 27 meter depth in bunker/satellite areas. I suggest they allow you to bring some drinks with you, and naturally allow you to regenerate your endurance - either fully or halfway with the upgrade system making it even quicker.
2. The drill - the upgrades increase the radius and speed at which you can dig through dirt, although at tier 4 it didn't feel that dramatic. At some point it feels like you have a high powered blow dryer and not a drill.

There is a day cycle with the game and the timer is rather quick. There was just a recent update that on a reduced setting, the day lasts twice as long. By 2300 you'll get a warning that night is coming and you have to navigate all the way back up to the top of the gas station and start shooting mutants, which appear at 2400/0000. I found that each round of full killing the mutants took up 3 or so game hours (it feels like 1 real world second is 2 game minutes). On days its raining you'll get a message that mutants won't be coming out, so you'll almost have 48 game hours to dig. I've never seen it rain 2 consecutive nights in a row.

Once in awhile an alien ship comes by midday to kidnap your dog. You have to stop what you're doing and shoot the UFO with a rifle you find at some point, or the turret. There's a planned update to stop these incursions at a certain point, because it can also get annoying. I'm not even sure why it's even in the game.

I haven't quite finished the game yet but purchased all the upgrades and it looks like I have one final task left. I'd recommend the game but be wary if you might find this constant back and forth annoying or not, I think the devs plan to alleviate this in the very near future. At least there should be a gameplay option for endurance regeneration.

4/12/26: Just finished the game and another gripe for me is the jetpack recharge rate (the jetpack is a mechanic to bring you back to the surface to save your game, drop items etc. You seem to get some kind of new digging tool at the very end but there doesn't appear to be a way to use it, nor is there a new game+.  I'm not interested in starting all over again due to the endurance mechanic, and at the beginning of the game it becomes very annoying. After all the upgrades are purchased its alleviated a lot but still annoying with the back and forth.

Крайне рекомендую! Игра по сути копия One Man´s Trash, только на максималках и с кучей других аспектов. Начнём:
1) Защита нашей базы. Пушки прокачиваются, количество пушек, урон, модификации увеличиваются. Всё увеличивается. Лопата, джетпак, здоровье и т.д. По сути, это главная фишка этой игры и она единственная с подобной тематикой копания и защиты базы.
2) Количество секретов, локаций и отсылок зашкаливает. Ближе к концу игры не так много, но первая половина игры просто поражает. Также в игре есть "черный" юмор. Если кому-то не нравится, можете выключить
Из минусов:
1) Не все достижения работают. Кто в теме, тот в теме. Я считаю, это позор. Также, почему нет достижения на нахождение всех сыров? На другие коллекционки они есть. Очень странный выбор, надеюсь со временем для новой аудитории эта халтура пофиксится разрабом.
2) Не нашёл последний артефакт. Может я как-то плохо искал, но хоть убей, я не смог. Желания гуглить вообще нет, к тому же игра только вышла, информации ноль.
3) Машина абсолютно бесполезная. Какой смысл от неё? Какой смысл пихать её части в яме, если толку от нее ноль?
4) Как и во многих таких играх, динамит здесь вообще бесполезный кусок сами знаете чего. Взрыв минимальный, зато ачивка есть с ним...
5) Радар здесь тоже вообще мусор. Также интересует, почему очень много предметов находится за пределами ямы в текстурах стен? Зачем они вообще там? Зачем радар их показывает?
6) Зачем в игре ружьё? Чтобы отбиваться от НЛО? Я могу это сделать пушкой на базе. Зачем этому уделяется вообще квест в яме, чтобы открыть этот бесполезный мусор? Ружьё не убивает врага в "лабиринте" даже.
7) В игре не хватает как минимум ещё половины улучшений, этапа 2-3. Копать яму очень долго, особенно для тех, кто копает в таких играх яму полностью, не оставляя ничего. Сразу отбило желание так делать. У игры нет лейт гейма вообще. Ресурсы копаешь, а тратить их некуда. Зато ачивку на 5000 монстров сделали, супер.
Несмотря на такое количество минусов описанных мною, игра мне крайне понравилась. Поначалу относился к ней скептически. По фоткам на странице с игрой плохо понятно было, что это, башенная защита или копалка.

[h3]掘りとタワーディフェンスゲー[/h3]
クリアーまではプレイしたのでレビューします。
大多数の時間は掘り、夜にちょっとタワーディフェンスという感じのゲームです。
リリース直後は他の掘りゲーでも何度も繰り返されてきた簡悔要素でぶっ叩かれまくってましたが、大分改善してプレイしやすくなったと思います。
レビュータイトルを[b]「親を掘りゲーに殺された作者が作った掘りゲー」[/b]としようかと思ったほどのマジで簡悔嫌がらせ要素満載のゲームでした。
パッチが来るまでは、掘りに期待していたのに明らかにタワーディフェンスの方がおもろいし、もう掘るのやだな、止めようかなと思ってたらパッチで継続プレイする気になりました。
ちなみに、タワーディフェンスといいつつ砲台FPSみたいになっており、効率よくヘッショをバシバシ決められてタワーディフェンス部分は初期から爽快です。
1000円超えてますが、今なら概ね値段分の価値はあるかなと思います。パッチ前なら3/10、今なら6.5/10くらいはあるかなと思います。


[u][b]良い点[/b][/u]
・掘った資源で成長し掘りを有利に進めるという基本はできています。初期は歴代屈指の糞オブ糞レベルのバランスでしたが現在のバランスならプレイは楽しいと思います。
・加えてタワーディフェンス部分の強化要素があります。タワーディフェンス部分は初期から効果も十分に感じられる成長具合で幅広く楽しめてよい点だと思います。
・宝探しゲー的なコレクターアイテム集め要素があり、良いアクセントになっていますが、ここは人によっては好みが分かれそうです。純粋な掘りゲーを楽しみたい人にとっては、掘り以外の探索は邪魔かもしれません。
・アスレチック要素があり、自分はまーまー楽しめたんですが、キー操作であることを考えると、ここでほどほど詰まる人がいるかもしれません。人によってはキレそうな要素です。
・日本語ローライズは及第点でゲームには支障はほぼないレベルだと思います。ただし、ちょっと理解しにくいときはあります。
・ハングアップしたりすることはなく問題なくゲーム継続できました。


[u][b]悪い点[/b][/u]
・仕様かバグがわかりませんが、画面解像度等の設定が毎度リセットされているようです。このゲームをプレイすると、既存のアプリやウィンドウ設定がとんでもないことになり、かなりの迷惑です。
・現金を使った博打要素がありますが、正直これやってるより掘ってる方が期待値高そうだし楽しいだしで、この要素要る？って感じでした。
・簡悔嫌がらせ要素にペットのアブダクションがありますが、正直これも要るか？って感じです。おそらくこの要素を楽しんだ人は世界で製作者だけでしょう。

I truly have no idea how this game managed to get so many "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews.
First, most of the gameplay consists of nothing but digging tunnels, which is extremely tedious and torturous. All the interesting minigames shown in the trailers are basically all the content there is—nothing more.Second, the promotional materials are extremely misleading and do not reflect the actual game at all.Third, charging ¥48 (or ¥36 on sale) for such an experience is unreasonable. While the models may look decent, the actual gameplay and content feel extremely cheap and unpolished.
Good news
Locations underground are preset and not randomly generated. You can get maps from experienced players.
Bad news
The QQ community is poorly managed. Admins heavily favor old beta players, forcing new players into a secondary group with almost no active support.
The gameplay loop is grueling. The shovel has a very small digging radius. Without a map, you may have to dig blindly in all directions to find the next structure.
The Tier 1 drill upgrade actually slows down overall digging speed significantly and only becomes usable with stamina upgrades.
The drill’s "auto-dig" description is misleading. You still have to hold the left button to dig slowly.
The game is nothing like the trailer. Zombies only appear in small numbers at night, making combat unsatisfying. UFOs and intense action are barely present.
The game is filled with meaningless rare collectibles. Completing all achievements requires digging nearly the entire underground area, which is pure grind.
Turrets are completely ineffective for automatic defense. Even fully upgraded, they cannot handle hordes. Zombies easily get stuck in blind spots and destroy your base.
The building and upgrade system is designed purely to force grinding. Resource costs are excessive, only meant to artificially prolong playtime.
Difficulty modes only tweak numbers to make grinding worse. Higher difficulties spawn far more zombies, while turrets remain weak without full upgrades. The only suggested strategy is to mindlessly dig for hours to upgrade everything at once.
Summary
The game is tedious, unbalanced, and fails to deliver on its promises. It feels like a half-baked grindfest that prioritizes padding playtime over actual fun.

review:
I love it. I saw it on "worth a buy" youtube channel and It actually was worth a buy! It's all I expected it to be and exactly what it says in the description. A lot of digging games get boring after a while because there are no stakes. No pressure or reason to complete the game once you killed 2 or three hours. This one breaks up the monotone dig loot upgrade dig... gameplay with a bit of zombie murder. And blowing-up zombies is always fun (if done right, and Puppyroar Games nailed it). 
The price is right for a 20-30 hours game  (normal difficulty without rushing. I am also stalling a bit before the end-game, but I'm very close after my time in the game) 

(note: I wrote this review before v1.0.4)

The good:
- Killing zombies is very satisfying. The gun-feel and the death animations are spot on.
- ♪ "I am a (Biker?) and I'm digging a hole / Diggy diggy hole / Digging a hole" ♪ :P
- Simple mechanics and precise controls
- Polished and consistent models and graphics (everything looks and feels like being a part of that world)
- Appropriate soundtrack
- The change from digging to killing feels natural and neither part feels tedious or gimmicky.
- The skill tree is extensive and well-thought. I didn't feel like any of the upgrades were useless or tiny incrementals. 
- Bonus hidden items to collect
- The story, (as much as you can say there is one) intrigued me. 
- Funny and low-brow humour (which you can actually switch off!), but it isn't intrusive at it did get a chuckle from me now and then. 
- No crashes, no game-breaking bugs and  no frame drops (It's a unbelievable that I have to actually consider this, but we live in a world where v1.0 means pre-alpha - not the case here, though).
- 4 updates in 4 days with real fixes - The devs seem to care about their game.

The bad:
- You don't "scavenge the wasteland". You dig a hole. You roam the inside of a vertical tank filled with dirt and junk). Fun as that may be, the description is a bit deceiving.
- Veteran difficulty (aka normal) is too easy. If you're a good shot and upgrade your base before anything else on each tier, there's almost no challenge. The zombies are just a (welcome) distraction from digging, but can be completely ignored in the mid-game. 
- if no framerate limit is set, it will max-out your GPU in the menu (but this is a common UE bug that can be easily fixed in future updates and I'm knit-picking).
- WIND ROSE's "Diggy Diggy Hole" is NOT on the soundtrack! :P

review:
Alors, je viens de finir le jeu.
Pour faire simple, il est bien, mais il y a quelques mécaniques un peu simplistes. Malgré un arbre de compétences varié, les attaques sont très répétitives et absolument pas stressantes.

Le minage est sympa, mais un peu inutile : tu farms beaucoup, mais les monuments que tu découvres sont sans grand intérêt. Tu vas trouver 2-3 améliorations intéressantes, mais ça reste surtout du farm intensif.

Je m’attendais à plus de surprises, notamment avec plusieurs types d’ennemis. Les aliens, par exemple, sont assez inutiles.

Au final, le jeu est bon, mais il manque de contenu à mon goût.

This is not Early Access. Therefore I will review it for what it is right now:
You get about 5 hours of fun for your $10. If thats fine for you I can recommend the game.
The digging and upgrade loop works fine and is fun, just like any other game of this type.
Some of the story elements/challenges that you encounter are also pretty cool and definitely needed to break up the core loop. But there aren't that many.

Minor spoilers below:

Other than that though the game is a bit disappointing, because I expected much more. While there are some elements that could bring some replayability value (branching upgrade choices) in the end they are not really changing anything and only artificially forcing replays from you. Calling that a roguelike feature just because the choice there is random is ridiculous. This game is not a "roguelike" and not a "Tower Defense". I dont care what my turret at home is doing, whether it's overpowered in way A or B. The enemies are killed either way. Beyond the first couple of nights you dont even have to fight the enemies yourself at all anyway. Maybe at higher difficulties, but not on the default one. Sadly this part is just filler and would quickly become boring so it's good that you can upgrade your way out of it. But obviously it would be better if it was a deeper feature that in itself is fun.

Regarding the digging: Again, the first time you are playing it is fun to explore underground and dig around, but in following playthroughs you will already know everything. It's not procedurally generated. You also have little choice on how to approach things and only the depth matters. Horizontally you dont get a lot of choice anyway and it doesnt matter where or how you dig you will find plenty of loot everywhere. There is literally no reason to use the scanning features.

Technically the game is decent. Performance is fine. It looks ok. For an unreal game I expected more visual fidelity but at least I didn't experience any majors technical issues. I guess they chose the right third-party unreal plugins. I wouldve liked to see better ultrawide support though. The corner-anchored UI makes it not work well on ultrawide so I had to limit my resolution to 16:9.

Lastly regarding my dissapointment: You get to find car parts to unlock a "car". And I expected that after having found all car parts you will unlock a car to travel to other areas where you can dig to explore even more stuff or maybe get to random dungeons or challenges or something. But no, all it is is another weapon in your arsenal. You can drive the car to attack enemies with. But there is literally no reason to do it. Mabye at higher difficulty levels you need to but I wouldn't because it's not fun anyway. It's hella slow, the terrain isnt made for it and using the main gun is more effective. And there are a bunch of  other weapons that you also can use instead. For example a drone or your rifle. This rifle is also a pretty dumb feature that in theory makes sense since you can upgrade your main gun to fire automatically, but the rifle sucks and ammo is extremely limited so that after one night you are out of ammo and for some reason there is literally no way to get additional ammo other than to find it. And that doesn't happen a lot. There are also zero upgrades for your gun. Another missed opportunity.

Finally there is also cash as currency that you can find throughout the scripted story in various underground bunkers and such. But it doesn't serve any purpose. Just another half-baked feature.

Additionally there are one-time use items to find when digging, some of which are pretty powerful, but there is no way to collect them and use them when you want and you also dont know what they will do unless you've played it before. There are also a couple of tools that you can craft and use actively (lamps and dynamite) but they both suck and have no further upgrades. Another missed opportunity.

There is also no way to customize your base and make it your own. You cant even put your gun where you want. It will always be teleported back on top of the roof of your base. Which is absolutely not where I want it. The base is basically just a bunch of wasted space with a couple of boring collectibles to find in the clutter.

I dont have any problem with the core game loop of digging, defending the base and having to get back to "drink" to restore energy/health every couple of meters. Yes that is repetitive and could be criticized but I know what I signed up for and it works alright. I also wont critize that you cant actively choose to drop some items in favor for others, because with a map as small as it is you dont run into major issues where you have to "maximize" your "dives". But I still wanted to mention it. Btw. I also dont mind the humor, it's a bit cringe but it's not making the game worse.

Overall this feels like a game made to cash in on the digging hype with a lot of half-baked features. And that's fine I guess, it's not a cash grab and it's not low quality. However it does give major Early Access vibes, while it is not. Would I have known this is only 5 hours of scripted gameplay with a pretty sudden and underwhelming ending and no major content updates lined up, I wouldnt have purchased it.

review:
The Spotter: Dig or Die is an excellent game that completely hooked me from the start. It’s incredibly fun, and even after about 10 hours of constant playtime—enough for me to beat the game—I still feel like there’s so much more left to discover. That’s one of its biggest strengths: it doesn’t feel “finished” in a limiting way, but instead like a world with a ton of room to grow.

The gameplay loop is satisfying, the progression feels rewarding, and there’s a great balance between challenge and creativity. Even after completing it, I found myself wanting to jump back in just to explore more and see what else I might have missed.

On top of that, the developers are very active and supportive in the Discord, which makes a huge difference. It’s clear they care about the game and the community, and that makes me even more excited about its future.

All in all, it’s a well-rounded experience that already delivers a lot, with strong potential to become something even greater. I’m really looking forward to seeing where this game goes next.

unhappily, I don't recommend. I ask myself, if I knew what this game was before I played, would I have wanted to invest the hours? I came back with a no. Read on for those of you with the digging autism.

It's about digging primarily as that is where you are spending most of your time; it's satisfying to  dig in a way which allows you to get back up in a pattern of your devising.  As you get deeper and deeper, your man-made bridges become their own landmarks for you to find your way back up with and there is a deep sense of satisfaction to that.

The turret defense part of the game is satisfying at first, but it's such a relatively short part of the game that comes so often that it very quickly becomes an annoyance. Eventually you can automate yourself out of caring about it with the right setup. I ended up skipping that portion of the game for a long while as the mutant waves' difficulty is seemingly tied to your own progression and does not appear to get increasingly harder, at least not in a way that a completely automated defense system can't handle.  After enough upgrades from digging, the defense system could be left alone night after night while I just continued digging. You can even set things up so that you never have to return to the surface for resource deposits or energy restoration.

That's the thing: the upgrades (save one very important one) invalidate parts of the game in a pleasing manner, but, especially in the case of the turret defense portion, the question must be asked "are those annoyances even necessary in the game if they fall to the level of 'annoyance'?" I feel like the upgrades should increase the fun, not  invalidate a part of the game like turret defense.

Anyway, on to my major complaint: the digging.

The digging is a vybe and if you know you like it, you know you like it. My issue is that the progression of the digging upgrades in this game do not match the usefulness of progression of the other upgrades. For example, you 
 can unlock the option to get 3 tiny sticks of dynamite which pale in comparison to the power of the random mines you run into beneath the earth. There is no better version of dynamite and it quickly stops becoming useful for the price. Worse, your shovel upgrades (which eventually become a drill) appear to be linearly more useful on the lower end of the spectrum. Often times you can't tell if one upgrade is that much more useful than the one you had before. Towards the tier 3 part of the game, this makes digging an extremely annoying timesink instead of the joy which is the central draw of the game.

I quit at tier 4 when I saw there were no more digging upgrades; it was too much of a slog to gather resources becauase, while digging ability proceeds in a series of small incremental upgrades, the amount of resources required for each upgrade is exponential. Not fun.
developer_response:
Thank you for such a detailed and thoughtful review, we really appreciate the time you took to break down different aspects of the game.

We’re glad to hear that the core digging experience and the sense of progression as you go deeper resonated with you, as this was one of the main pillars we focused on.

We also understand your concerns about the balance between digging and base defense. From the start, defense was intended as a secondary layer to add tension and variety, not as the main focus, but we see how it can start to feel repetitive, especially in later stages.

Thank you as well for the feedback on upgrades, especially regarding dynamite and tool progression. These are valuable points, and we are already looking into ways to make upgrades feel more impactful in the later parts of the game.

We are a small team, and finding the right balance between depth and pacing is an ongoing process for us. Feedback like yours really helps us understand where things can be improved.

Thanks again for sharing your experience 🙏

review:
[h1]Creuser le jour, survivre la nuit[/h1]

Dig or Die

Dig or Die est un petit jeu sans prétention qui mélange exploration, minage et défense de base. Sur une courte durée, il propose une boucle simple mais efficace, parfaite pour une session chill sans prise de tête.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

Le gameplay alterne entre deux phases : explorer et miner pour récupérer des ressources, puis défendre sa base contre les vagues d’ennemis. Ce petit twist fonctionne bien et donne un rythme agréable au jeu.

On reste cependant sur quelque chose de assez classique. Les mécaniques sont simples, faciles à prendre en main, et ne cherchent pas à réinventer le genre. Mais ça marche, surtout sur une courte durée.

Construire ses défenses, améliorer son équipement et optimiser un minimum sa base apporte juste ce qu’il faut de réflexion sans devenir trop complexe.

[h3]Histoire[/h3]

L’histoire est basique et sert surtout de contexte. Elle fait le travail sans marquer particulièrement.

[h3]Durée de vie[/h3]

Le jeu se termine en environ 4 heures, ce qui est parfaitement adapté à ce qu’il propose. Il ne s’étire pas et reste agréable du début à la fin.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]

Dig or Die est un petit jeu chill, simple et efficace. Il ne brille pas par son originalité, mais son mélange mine/défense fonctionne suffisamment bien pour offrir une expérience agréable sur quelques heures.

Un bon petit jeu à faire tranquillement, sans en attendre plus que ce qu’il propose.

临时解决方案

BIOS 设置
Windows AI 设置
我们目前正与Epic Games（虚幻引擎开发商）保持联系，以寻求妥善的解决方案。 在此之前，禁用NPU是目前唯一可靠的解决办法。

Over all, probably better than most "digging a hole" games, but still over all simply lacking. 

You have a standard loop, find loot, upgrade equipment, dig further. This one you must return to the surface every so often to fight off waves of mutants. While try to accomplish both, it does neither overly good. 

Digging:
Pro - Unique loot to collect (cans and bicycles in stead of usual ore), they are physics object so they interact with the world and move around as you dig (not solid so pass right through), abundant placement of basic materials, interesting secrets to find and models to discover. Various fun powerups to find throughout your digging.

Cons - Shovel feels very weak compared to other games. Manual digging feels okay but the auto/drill feels so slow and small. If developer increased this (perhaps moving every upgrade functionality down the tree) it would feel much better. Physics objects means once your inventory is full, you can't see past them and get in the way. The models you can find are VERY solid and often times impede progress. that's the point on some of them, but when digging is unfulfilling with the previously mentioned shovel, much more of a pain than and gameplay mechanic. No way to easily find secrets without *excessively* digging around. Powerup should be permanent. There is no reason to have a temporary backpack expansion that only lasts a few minutes.

Combat:
Pro - Various main gun types to choose from. Multiple upgrades to enhance survivability and different tools to use in the fight.

Con - Tedious, simple, rather unengaging. The car mentioned in the trailer you only get very late into the game, extremely low on gas so doesn't last long. With enough upgrades you'd think it can last on it's own but no, you still need to babysit it. The hand held gun is mostly useless with limited findable ammo. 

Misc
Pro - Doggy :), Slot machine, basketball, seek and find hidden items, cute original songs on radio

Con - Aliens take your dog :(, which turns out to be a good thing, but when the song on the radio literally say "don't let the aliens take your dog," it makes it feel very frustrating when your down in the mine and you get an alert the they are coming and you literally cannot get back in time so save it so you restart the day. No way to earn money for the slot machine aside from finding cash and killing mutants (once a day during night raid). Basket ball has flat physics, feels bad to throw. Always that one thing you can't find in a collection.

The ending started out epic but then turned rather disappointing. Also the graphics are a choice, I enjoy them, but I can easily see them turning some people away. Neither positive or negative in this regard.

So overall, while the game is good, and arguably the most fleshed out of this style, the issues it has simply overtake the good.

I tried this during NextFest and ended up not recommending it for unavoidable and obnoxious amounts of juvenile/toilet humor, but decided to give it a shot since I saw the developers added an option to turn it off. To be clear, it doesn't remove everything: the game still opens with an extended pooping scene, right-clicking makes you pee, some items make you vomit, etc. However, with the option toggled off it's reduced to a much more manageable level than the NextFest demo at launch.

Overall the core gameplay loop is engaging. Digging and exploring feels rewarding, the tower defense combat is fun, and trying to balance upgrades for both creates some interesting prioritization. The progression path feels pretty smooth and while none of the upgrades/powers radically change the game they all feel like they're working towards a shared endgoal and feel rewarding. 

Overall there's some minor quibbles and issues I have with certain mechanics, but for <$10 I can't really complain. Additionally, it's clear the devs are paying very close attention to feedback and working very quickly to make improvements and changes, so I assume the game will only get better over time. 

Consider me a convert!

I dug out the whole hole, and in the ending video you get a new shovel, but you can't even use it, because you have to load an older save to "continue" playing.
A very mixed bag this game. It is "just" another game about digging a hole but with a bit of base defense every ~2 days and some underground puzzles. And for 13€ I cannot recommend it.

The devs are still working on the game though and one thing that bothered me was fixed in 1.0.4, which is 2 days after release, so I think the game might get there from a quality standpoint.

What annoyed me the most is the teasing of things that could be but never are, like;[list]
[*] The fact that you find enough parts for your car to build two, but even a single car is useless, it's only another weapon to help in the defense of the night, you can't even drive to Las Vegas like the map shows, not even after you complete the game.
[*] After you complete the game you have to load the auto save like you never completed it, making the game actually worse after seeing the end.
[*] The drill upgrades are all quite useless after the first one, you can barely see the difference between the first and last drill.
[*] A carry capacity of only 3 dynamite, their non-upgradable explosion radius and slippiness makes them quite useless if you have a drill and some endurance upgrades. (Flying back up takes longer than keeping on drilling)
[*] Some turret upgrades make the turret feel worse.
[*] Why can't I switch my ultimates? Even for the money it would have cost to buy a new one.
[*] At least make the travel to Las Vegas possible in a DLC down the line.
[*] Why do I have to get my dog adopted to 100% achievement this game? Quite cruel.
[*] Put the keys the NPCs give you in the player inventory at the end of the conversation so that you don't have to go back down to the jump scare mirror in the DJ room.
[*] I thought I exploded the end of the vine on my play-through because it looks "cut off" making the end pointy would fix that for anyone who used too much dynamite like me.
[*] Please add a volume slider for the main char, his jumping voice really is annoying after 10 hours.
[*] A Spider enemy in the spider mine and the sword dude being killable would go a long way in making the gun actually useful. It would also literally be a blast to be able to mine with the gun, it having a reload mechanic and forgeable ammo like dynamite and lamps would make it a nice addition to the game and it being upgradable and a real alternative to classic mining alone would make this game stand out even more. There is no game about shooting a hole. (Except maybe the first Red Faction) :)

[h3]And the worst of them all:[/h3]
[*] Please make it so that the floating objects cannot be fully dug out, it looks very bad and simply moving them a bit to the edge so that they are in the hard stone barrier or hung by the steel beams would go a long way! The skeleton for example is already attached to the wall and some cars are being held the steel beams.
[*] Also it is strange to have dirt stuck the roof in a concrete or steel construction why is it up there? The distribution of diggable material is very unrealistic and unimmersive, it makes the game look rushed and cheap.
[/list]
developer_response:
Thank you for your review. I’d like to note that we carefully read and consider feedback from all players, and many community suggestions are already part of our development plans.

We’ve already started working on the Las Veganos city, and you will be able to travel there by car. I won’t spoil what’s waiting there. We also have planned upgrades for dynamite so its explosion radius can be increased.

Regarding turrets feeling worse, that issue has already been fixed. As for the dog, you can rescue it after it gets taken, and once you do, the UFO will no longer appear. Adding keys directly to the inventory is also planned.

Good point about the cut-off vine, we’ve already fixed that as well. For the main character’s voice, there is already an option to disable those sounds.

We originally planned to add a spider to the mine but didn’t have time before release. It will be added in the future, the whole web location was actually designed with that in mind. The sword guy can now be killed with weapons, this was added in a recent patch.

As for the floating objects, we agree, and we’ll review where this happens and make it feel more natural.

I also want to mention that we are a small team of four developers. As you can see, we are listening to the community and actively implementing many of the requested changes.

Thank you again for your feedback, it’s genuinely valuable to us. We hope you’ll return to the game in the future, see how it has improved, and maybe reconsider your review.

I'm calling it, for the 10$ I paid, this is well (WELL) worth a buy. Spotter plays as advertised. You dig for scrap, upgrade your base, and at night battle zombies. This game scratches that [i]"Turn off your brain and listen to a podcast"[/i] Itch. Digging 50+ feet underground finding; magical items, jewels, hidden bunkers, etc. is all extremely staisfying.

[b] Pro's; [/b] [list]

[*] Level progression is perfectly balanced with meaningful upgrades.

[*] Killing zombies at night is fun and breaks up digging time perfectly.

[*] The timer adds a level of heart pounding fun I didn't think the devs could pull off.

[*] Graphics, sound, optimization are flawless.

[/list]

[b] Pro's; [/b] [list] 

[*] Perks like Vacuum are somewhat clunky. Controls in general take a little getting use to. And I'm finding using both my controller and keyboard is the only way to go.

[*] Poor tutorials. I received a key that's supposed to open an office and no explanation as to why it's not doing so. 

[*] Time controls can leave you feeling there's not enough time to explore. Like digging must be done to mine resources (upgrades) for the next zombie wave.

[*] You need to keep up on manual saves because one bad night will have you starting all over. It's a game where you need to learn, restart your entire run, then learn some more. I like it, but some will hate the need to plan for an event that will happen several hours into the future.

[/list]

review:
我非常推荐这款游戏，玩了8个小时通关了，游戏非常爽快，挖地找宝物的感觉很爽，升级基地打怪就一般般。
游戏引导还算可以，前期可以顺着藤曼挖，后面的地堡难找，跳跳乐幸好流程短，再往沿着修电线可以电线一路挖就可以，最后地底有一圈矿道虽然入口很多，但是很难找。
此外还有很多建议改进的：
1.篮球太难了，成就12米投篮需要借助疾跑，我最多11.4m蒙中的，还总是不知道为什么判作弊。拿篮球时给个准星，篮筐扩大一点比较好。
2.游戏基地的火箭非常吵，电磁炮有时候音效也突然发出坏掉一样的声音很吵，在地下也听得到。总之游戏音效我很不满意。
3.电缆室缺引导，而且我当时被吓坏了，按了按钮没反应我已急哭，然后看到门上有数字才知道要按一百多下开一扇门，但是有四扇门需要分别按一百多下，我裂开了，还要躲避追杀。
4.中后期基地武器的提升感知不强，像伤害，射速，弹夹容量，冷却什么的由于机枪子弹多，伤害高，射速快，提升的感觉不强，反倒因为音乐吵，音效吵，搞得不是很想手操打怪，只想升级全自动的炮塔，火箭弹。
5.扫描仪太逆天了，前期范围短，显示时间短，而且挖的慢，很容易忘记标点，但还是很好用。后期范围大，显示时间还是短，但是资源很多，一扫下去一百多个绿点看瞎了，我都不知道哪个近哪个远，我建议扫描仪最终升级变成一直显示资源，可以随意开启关闭，范围可以调小一点。
6.炸弹非常好用，但是可以升级多带几个或者加爆炸范围就好了。炸弹有的时候会卡bug掉下去。
7.车子修好了但是不知道怎么用，好像说要给车装电磁炮。
不是很有兴趣打全成就，篮球太逆天了，剩下的就是时间问题慢慢磨，很多成就很无聊。
很感谢这款游戏带给我很多快乐，游戏很好玩。

The game is amazing! I’m honestly shocked. Thought I’d play for like 30 minutes just to check it out, but now I’m actually going to finish it.

What really got me is the loop. You go down to mine, tell yourself “okay, just a bit more,” and suddenly it’s night and you’re barely ready, scrambling to survive. That tension works really well.

Also didn’t expect to enjoy the base defense this much. Setting everything up is one thing, but when things start going wrong and you have to jump in yourself, it gets intense fast.

The upgrades feel meaningful too. It’s not just small stat boosts, you can really feel your build changing how you approach each run. Sometimes you play safe, sometimes you go full chaos and just hope it works.

And yeah, there’s that “one more run” effect. Every time you fail, it feels like you could’ve done better with a slightly different plan, so you just go again.

Didn’t expect to get hooked like this, but here we are.

Enjoyable game. Finished it in about 7 hours. There are a few different loadouts you can go for the late game upgrades, so if you want to try a different combat style you can replay it.

Honestly, I’m a bit surprised this game even has negative reviews. The team behind it is clearly very small, and considering that, what they’ve managed to build is seriously impressive.

At first, I thought it would be just another “dig by day, shoot by night” indie mix, but it hooked me way more than I expected. The contrast feels great: during the day you’re calmly digging, planning, being greedy for “just one more run”… and then night hits and everything turns into chaos.

One of the best parts is that you’re not just placing turrets and watching. At the peak moments, you actually take control and defend the base yourself, which makes it feel much more intense and personal.

The progression system is also solid. Different playstyles actually feel different, not just like number changes. One run you’re precise and careful, the next you’re turning the battlefield into pure destruction with rockets and traps. Artifacts can completely change how the game plays, which keeps runs fresh.

Yeah, there are some rough edges. Sometimes the balance feels a bit off, and it’s not always clear whether you lost because of your mistake or just bad luck. But considering the size of the team, it’s really not a big issue.

Overall, it’s a very addictive and well-thought-out hybrid. You’ve got both chill and action, and a strong sense of progression. Definitely worth checking out if you like the idea of preparing by day and surviving by night.

[h1][b]报告长官！我只在铁屑里面发现了一点泥土！[/b][/h1]
[i]李诞在《冷场》还是《笑场》里面写过一个很臭屁且无厘头的故事，大概意思是指一个男人在自己的公寓楼里突发癔症，幻视地板中央有一个红叉，就此认定下面买着秘宝，于是就像饥饿站台层层陷落一样挖掘，部分邻居也随之魔怔，就这地板自认为的标记死命的挖掘。[/i]
[i]初看的时候就觉得又是李诞既水又是其不明其厉文风的一种体现，在他笔下人都是事不获己地做些出格地举动，然后用一些西部公路片的感觉收回来。[/i]
[b]但是等等，这次给我干哪来了。[/b]
轮到我开始成为着魔的村民，废土末世，虽然以总统作为最高行政长官的政治体还在，但对于我而言，似乎离得太远了，我能听见的是远在天边告诉我不要放弃，等待总统救援的任务无线电波和……近在耳边的变异体嘶鸣。
好在还是白天，揉揉眼睛，前面一块空地，还有红叉，手边还有铲子，挖掘是以力换物的买卖，索性，当我们在焦土中挖出深浅不一麻点般的铲坑中搜出物资，需将之放于旁边的回收机变为相应的矿资，这些通货用来强化总计[b]四阶各有不同的技能树[/b]，譬如以挖养挖，接下来挖掘的坑洞更大，背包库存更大，如深挖还需解锁喷气背包傍身；又如以挖养战，到了夜里与变异体交锋前，我们只有一门主炮，加速换弹等增益逐夜减少火力缺失而生的恐慌；或者以挖供生，让自己减少挖一会就得续上液体手雷的欲望、或者夜间增加可见光。
总之，这是一套相对扎实的即时反馈逻辑，挖了就有用，有用后可以更加持续且变强的挖，当然，本作没有增量游戏的爽点。
[b]因为打僵尸确实不太容易。[/b]
当左上角的时间条逼向血红的深夜，泛绿的变异体破土而出，玩家需要从栖居地的外立面攀援而上，搭上炮台，像4399《狙击小某本》那样360度点杀僵尸。
其实击杀的感觉还是比较好的，打击感一般但是爆头的图标回馈还不错，比较要命的还是初始弹匣有限的同时换弹较久，这会产生[b]越慌越马，越马越慢，越慢越慌[/b]的恶性循环，虽然第二天我们可以用铁资源进行基地血量回复，但是前期的低容错会让马枪几次就基本上预示败局，本质还是第二关的某几个幻视二爷的狂乱僵尸砸门速度太快了。
[b]徒有日夜循环的区分玩法刺激还不够，还需要有末世彩蛋。[/b]
日有日活，夜有夜战，白天为了夜晚蓄势，夜晚有为了玩家直抵下一个明天的玩法让我感到《牧场物语风之集市》的肝疼，这种逻辑本质上是一种讨巧的转换玩家新鲜感锚点的做法，但如果没有比较本质休闲的玩法或者一些额外彩蛋的新鲜感，前述左脚踩右脚会在中期就开始变得枯燥。
于是本作加入了一些老虎机、篮球的彩蛋/非主要核心增益的玩法，为了控制玩家挖矿的节奏，还设置了探宝器进行特殊物品的图鉴收集（但是实际体验特别积累，探宝功能要求玩家集中一点登封造极，但是强化能力的前期尽量让我们在浅表就雨露均挖，于是，不妨就当探宝不存在）。
当然矿产类型上的丰盈、塔防系统的强化也会有，可玩性方面的增加还是比较有限的。

游戏现阶段的玩法就是死后局外增益的缺失，已有了难度分级，但是在最低的难度本质还不算太休闲，而且死后缺乏了局外增益会让人觉得，每一次重开游戏都是从零开始的上一句，虽然游戏内置了自动保存，可以回到上一周目，但是如果一定要让自己回到上一周目最后一天绞劲脑汁苦苦支撑，倒不如允许玩家在局外增益之后，看上去没有那么重复的开下一个周目。
我觉得，增加一个最低级的难度，保留上一周目的全部强化，倒也不错，前期的塔防狙僵尸也可以稍爽些，换弹期对于我这个fps苦手确实可能没那么友好。
但是本作确实给了一个比较不错的制式的游戏体验，不说顶尖，至少前期的收集狙击交错有致。

《丧尸末世：地底全是财，挖宝造炮台》在这个丧尸末世的世界里，你找到了一座废弃的加油站作为你的据点，开局只有一把小铁锹，东西全靠挖，白天你需要不断的向地下深处挖掘，通过拾取里面的垃圾来进行到机器里置换铁，开局背包不大体力不多，你只能快速的往返，当你挖掘到一定程度后是会没有体力的，这时候就需要来一瓶冰镇爽快啤酒来缓解回复体力并且在宝贵的时间里获得更多资源。

[h2]游戏玩法[/h2]

除了盲目的往下挖之外，你还拥有探测器，可以进行搜寻附近高价值的物品，这也确实便利了许多，不仅如此，你觉得你挖掘的地板坑坑洼洼的不妨可以来尿一手，随着你不断的挖掘，时间也是过得飞逝，到了夜晚则是丧尸会入侵你的据点，你需要到达你的顶楼使用武器进行防守，据点也是有着血量不过前期也是比较简单，因为你的电台等级比较低所以难度不高，打怪也是有技巧的可以打头这样可以更快速的过完，并且打怪也是会掉落钞票可以到机器上进行娱乐小赌，虽然可能会让你一无所有。

挖掘是一件十分有意思的事情，你不断的下挖，可能会有一些限时道具，也可能有更高价值的资源，亦或者你可能挖到一个庇护所，这时候你就需要通过寻找适配的道具进行解开开始探索，里面可能会有一个类似额外专属奖励的，可以根据自己所需来选择，可以短期也可以长远根据自己的眼光来。

不仅如此，游戏内还有着升级系统，比如铲子的范围速度，体力恢复，喷漆背包等，每个等级都是由限制的，前面基本上只需要铁，当你到了第二阶段后不仅怪物变多难度变高，甚至所需的物资是金块，对于前期来说是很困难，但是只需要一直挖掘总会有概率挖到一片，除了庇护所，可能还有汽车配件等，不过这个也是比较后面的东西了。

天赋科技升级可以设置炮塔给你减轻压力，只能说里面的有趣东西不少，随着你不断升级到后期只能说你这个据点变得非常强大，甚至可以白天黑夜进行采集，游戏内也有着小彩蛋，狗子会陪伴着你，也可能会被外星人抓走，甚至与可能有一些特殊玩偶摆件等着你去收集。

[h2]总结[/h2]

游戏整体体验下来是一款非常不错的，你不仅白天需要挖宝，夜晚还需要进行防守尸潮，而且地下的各种彩蛋也是非常的多，前面的手动到后期的高伤害的炮塔，还能开车，甚至于可以尿尿，这些都非常有意思，游戏非常推荐一定要体验！

review:
Okay so first things first I absolutely love this game and I just want to make that clear, everything feels very intuitive the AI upgrades are amazing and I think the balance reworks are great. However as someone who enjoys digging and collecting the relics, as the relics do tend to contain game changing assets that can either give you resources you desperately need or a new support utility of some sort which I love that.

 HOWEVER I am not fond of feeling like a tunnel rat trapped in a maze, as I consistently dig following what the note says..... And there is nothing but walls all around me and I can't even get to the relic, I respect and understand why the note isn't too specific. But it goes from fun and challenging to annoying, when I've spent several hours in just one area trying to configure out which direction.....

I definitely feel like the space should be more condensed and not so massive or at the very least have the entrance be easier to find. Cause for the past several hours of my playthrough so far, has just been trying to progress past that puzzle and I got the rifle from the last puzzle and I thought the vine was a neat touch. But there isn't even like some sort of hint or anything. Going around is so vague and when I went around, I still could not progress I just kept hitting walls.... I'd feel my excitement climb as I feel like I might be progressing and then my spirit crushed as I find yet another wall... But that is just my biggest complaint so far and overall I think the game is really great.
