review:
I'm tentatively recommending this. I beat the game with about 5 hrs of playtime. I'm sure there's more to do (such as collecting the stuff), but I feel satisfied with my time with this game for now. I got it on a meager sale and was debating refunding it after 90 minutes of playtime as some things just irked me. The combat gameplay is middling, and the music sounds generic or even AI generated (not accusing here). The vibes were just off for me.
I went to reviews and read other peoples' feedback and some of the dev's responses. The top reviews didn't seem sincere to me (more of the kind of review you leave your friends), so I kept reading. The dev responses did seem honest and kind when they had the opportunity to be jerks. So, I waited a day or two to get back to this, and for the most part did enjoy my remaining time with the game.

Some further notes:
- The last antenna upgrade or two was definitely grindy. Maybe intentional. I wasn't totally fed up with the grind by the end, so maybe the balance is fine there.
- After a while (tier 3 or so of the antenna upgrade), I stopped having to come out of the mines. My combat upgrades and automated turret AI were holding the line at night. Not sure how I feel about it, but part of me desires that power fantasy where my base just kicks ass on its own. For a shorter game it's fine, but in the long run, it probably isn't a healthy approach to maintain if the devs want to expand this concept further, at least without some other drawbacks.
- I mostly ignored the upgrades like unlocking the Car, EMP stun, etc. Only ones relevant to me were the extra damage powerup (middle mouse button, because it was the first one I unlocked I think). And at times there seemed like too many buttons. I don't know if I used the dynamite at all. I definitely didn't use the sonar tracking beacon things. I felt better off leaving lights as visual cues for where to go to get back to the surface (or down to my main digging spot).
- The biggest gripe I would have is during the last sequence, I was told the nukes were dropping in 10 seconds. I hauled ass underground ASAP. I found the bunker earlier, and read that it said it will open during a nuclear launch event, so I figured I would need to find it later. Anyways - no hesitation. I get through the bunker and through the... secondary bunker? And it needs a keypad code. I have no idea what it wanted from me, until I die to the toxic gas and respawn on the surface. Hold on, is the surface not a dangerous place to be now? I check out the terminal and it says "here's your code, bozo" (maybe with some embellishment). Was I supposed to just wait through this ten second timer of a nuclear launch??? That was super panic inducing, I was NOT about to wait around for a code that I didn't even know existed until I was breathing in toxic gas!
- Definitely has some bugs. I get there are like 2 devs working on this, and I'm a software developer as well, so I get it. Sometimes the automated turret on the surface continues firing even after the waves end. I fixed it once by going in and messing around until it fixed itself. Second time however, when I got in and was messing around, I somehow killed myself (I was using the artillery turret with 3x firing mode upgrade). That was quite comical. I resurrected and was still in the turret view, and when I left I was in the main building.

Would recommend people get it when it's on sale. It's quirky with some spooky parts (weird ninja button room was super spooky for the first few seconds I was in there) and I can tell some heart was put into this. That's the main reason this is a recommendation. Just would appreciate some more variation on the music, a little bit of more variance in the gameplay (not more powerups please), and tidy up some parts of the experience (i.e. the final sequence).

[h1] 忙しい穴掘りが好きな人向け [/h1]
※難易度ノーマルクリア後の所感

よくある穴掘りゲームに、タワーディフェンス要素を加えた作品です。

最深部を目指して掘り進めている途中でエイリアンが襲来するため、防衛もしながら進める必要があり、かなり忙しいゲーム性になっています。そのため、「キープディギング系」のように穴掘りだけに集中したい人にはあまり向いていません。

そしてこのシステムの関係上、ジェットパックの管理にも注意が必要です。油断していると時間に余裕をもって地上へ戻れず、迎撃が間に合わないこともあり、掘削の時間管理も重要になってきます。

残念だった点として、AIに射撃を任せると逆に弱くなってしまう武器のパターンがありました (電撃ビーム)。いろいろ試したいのですが、一度改造したツリーを元に戻せない仕様のため、このあたりは改善してほしいところです。

また、オートセーブの数が１つしかないので、進行状況によっては詰む可能性もあります。現状では、次のティアに進む前に基地強化をできる限り進めておくのが無難でしょう。

賛否が分かれている作品ではありますが、個人的には非常に楽しめました。
唐突にイヌがUFOに連れ去られる、ドリルが全然削れないなどテンポの悪さは今後の改良に期待します。

「穴掘りしながらエイリアンも撃ちたい！忙しいけど楽しい！」という、アクティブに遊びたい人にはおすすめできるゲームです。

The game is super fun! The game loop of digging, finding things, selling it for scrap and buying upgrades really activates the dopamine circuits. I'm loving it and I must know what's hidden in the dirt!!!

Such a charming game! You spend time digging, then recycling what you find, and using those resources to upgrade yourself, your shovel, and your base. 

With the latest update, Las Veganos, there's TONS more to do and explore. It's actually incredible for what it is.

I recommend this game. It's fun and enjoyable with good content. For the price, its honestly a steal. You dig during the day for scrap to upgrade your tools/base, and then at night you defend against the zombies. I haven't ran into any bugs or issues.

The game is okay-ish. I would give it a neutral rating, if possible.

In around 5hrs, you can finish it (I guess, since I had around 8hrs), which is a bit too short for my tastings, regarding the price.

There are around three main parts of the game:
- battle phase (at night, where you have to man the turret and beat the zombies)
- dig & exploration phase (at day, where you have to search the ground for stuff)
- skill & base setup part, where you have to invest your resources into either building your base (which means to unlock base "skills") or to improve your gear/skills

The core loop is okay and enjoyable, although I did not like two parts of it:
1) your jetpack fuel is limited (per charge), so you have to take care about how to dig down, so you can get up, again to come back to your base. And no matter how, in the end, you will have a ground which looks like swiss cheese, which is a bit annoying
2) the days are relatively short and the travel to the underground (and back to the top, again, in time) gets longer, the longer you play, which shortens the dig part and enlargens the (boring) travel part, where you have to actually DO something. But it's manageable enough, tbh.

The fights at night are a bit monotone/boring, so I am happy that you can skill into AI turrets, which will eventually give you the possibility to ignore the nights, since the base defense will manage the attacks, without your presence. Of course, this will cost quite some invested resources, to get those skills.

The one thing I really hated about the game (and that is the reason why I stopped playing around 5min before the end scene) are 2-3 sections of the game, where you have to do some jump n run stuff, like dodging laser lines and jumping on poles, under time pressure. So I warn you, if you hate jump n runs, like I do. You cant evade those parts, since they are built into the main "quests" of the game.

In hindsight, I enjoyed the first 2hours of the game and the artstyle & setting is nice.
After that time, it became obvious that the game loop lacks some real variation and the mechanics dont go too deep (enough, imho).

If you like digging for stuff and want a bit action-pew-pew combined with that, this game might scratch that itch.
And I can really see kids loving that game, especially since it does not have too elaborated mechanics which are easy to learn.

[h1]Feedback[/h1]

The [b]energy system[/b] is one of the biggest issues in the game. When both energy and jetpack run out at the same time, getting back to the surface from deep underground becomes extremely frustrating and repetitive. After experiencing this multiple times, it really kills the motivation to keep playing. On top of that, getting attacked during these moments makes the situation even more stressful.

As a suggestion, it would be great if players could purchase and store [b]energy recovery items[/b] in their inventory using the money they collect. These items could restore energy instantly or over time, making the gameplay much smoother and less punishing.

[hr][/hr]

The [b]progression system[/b] also feels quite weak. Both the drill upgrades and other improvements lack depth. For a game centered around digging, this aspect should feel much more rewarding and diverse.

For example:

Add [b]character abilities[/b] tied to digging
Introduce a [b]skill tree system[/b]
Allow players to create different builds

These kinds of systems would add depth and significantly improve replayability.

[hr][/hr]

[b]For now, I’m leaving a negative review, but I hope these aspects will be improved in future updates.[/b]

这款游戏整体体验相当不错，值得推荐。

首先要说的是配乐表现非常出色，背景音乐与游戏氛围融合得很好，无论是挖矿建设时的轻松节奏，还是遭遇丧尸时的紧张感，都能通过音乐得到很好的烘托，沉浸感很强。

玩法上结合了挖矿、建造和对抗丧尸等元素，整体设计颇具创意。玩家既需要规划资源、拓展地下空间，又要随时应对丧尸的威胁，节奏张弛有度，过程相当有趣，也很容易让人一玩就停不下来。

不过目前也存在一些可以优化的地方。比如在挖土的模型上，范围判定略显模糊，很多时候不太容易判断具体能挖到哪里，缺乏清晰的边界反馈，这在一定程度上会影响操作的精准性和体验流畅度。

另外有一个比较有潜力的改进方向是，可以考虑加入“土方塌陷”的机制。当玩家过度挖空某一区域时，可能会触发塌方，不仅增加游戏的真实感，也能带来更多策略性，比如需要提前加固结构或合理规划挖掘路径，这样玩法层次会更加丰富。

总体来说，这是一款创意十足且完成度不错的作品，在保证趣味性的同时也有进一步打磨的空间，期待后续更新能带来更多优化和惊喜。

Dig a hole but with bunkers to find, a car to build, a dog to pet, and tower defense.

[h2] I have a problem [/h2]

That problem being that I own like, a goofy amount of simulator games. It’s obscene. I need help.

If you can think of a simulator game with controller support (I know, I know, M+KB master race, but, nerve damage is a thing), I almost certainly own it and have sunk an embarrassing amount of hours in it. My Steam Library says Elden Ring is my most played game, but, I think Supermarket Simulator and Shelldiver would like to have a word.

I’m always on the lookout for a title that does more than the norm, that goes that extra mile to distinguish itself from the herd, especially in an environment where once a game gains the attention of a big name content creator, a hundred also-rans come out by sundown trying to capitalize on that hype.

The Spotter: Dig or Die, is one such game that works to distinguish itself from the herd, and good gracious is it ever a lovely time!

[h2] So, what’s it all about? [/h2]

Some manner of outbreak has occurred and as a result, the world is overrun by mutants (see: zombies). There’s supposedly a bunker city where we’ll all be safe and we’ve got to power up our radio tower well enough to receive “The President’s message” advising us of how to access it.

The game is split into two and a half primary modes: digging, tower defense, and THE LORE.

[h2] The Spotter as a Simulation Game [/h2]


If you’ve played other digging based games, like “A Game About Digging a Hole”, then you know what to expect here, and that’s not necessarily a bad thing.

You start out with a tiny shovel that digs tiny holes and a backpack the size of a small almond that can only fit three things, and like any good incremental game, as you gather more scrap you turn it in for a variety of upgrades that make your life easier.

You get a radar partway into the tutorial to help point you to the good stuff, you upgrade to better shovels and eventually to other digging implements, you get a jetpack early on (which is great because there are a few places the game will absolutely let you soft-lock yourself, more on that in a bit), and all that and all that.

The pacing feels good here. Having played a ton of incremental/simulator games, they typically fall into one of four categories:

1. Titles like “a game about digging a hole” that are meant to be knocked out in an afternoon.
2. Titles like Shelldiver that sneak up on you where at first you feel quite underpowered, but before you realize it you’re tearing through the environment at a tremendously satisfying pace.
3. Titles like “Keep on Mining” that have you hit walls with a degree of frequency that can make progression feel like a slog
4. Titles like “A Game About Feeding a Black Hole” that are neither slow nor fast, but fit you just right, like a favorite pair of jeans.

The Spotter feels like it lands in the fourth category; the pacing feels good, the progression feels natural, and overall I don’t have much in the way of complaints.

Revisiting the controller support thing, I’ve got nerve damage that makes M+KB for sustained periods painful and a controller more managable, so I’m always on the lookout for (and often disappointed by the lack of) games in the genre that have native controller support. Before I offer any constructive feedback, let me just say thank you, sincerely, to the developers for considering those of us that either prefer, or in my case legitimately need, controller support.

For the most part, The Spotter does a great job with it, but both here and in the tower defense sequence I feel like it could use a bit more aim assist; it can be difficult to find the balance of “I need my camera to move fast enough that I don’t die” alongside “I need it to move slow enough that I can aim properly at what I’m picking up/shooting at”.

[h2] Speaking of shooting at things [/h2]

Oh, it’s wildly fun. Again, aiming with a controller could use some work (calm down, PC master race), a bit more aim assist would help, but overall it’s a great-ish experience.

[h2] Ish? [/h2]

So, about that “the game will let you soft lock yourself” thing, the tutorial encourages you to move at a rapid pace, but you can easily land yourself in a bad spot early on that you'll have difficulty recovering from. The loop is that during the day you dig, during the night you defend your base.

You purchase upgrades such as turrets, more powerful artillery and such, and it can feel rather punishing with how slow your manual gun reloads at first, but with some careful planning you can get around that. My advice is to ignore the tutorial for the first day or two, just gather a bunch of scrap so you can start out right away with a turret, quicker reload times for your rifle, etcetera.

The mutants don’t start attacking until you start repairing and building out your antenna, and there’s a cap on how aggressive each night gets until you reach the next milestone, but it’s a bit feast or famine right now. It’s not hard to end up unprepared and unable to progress if you're not careful, but the game does mitigate this somewhat with the save system.

The game autosaves at intervals and maintains a single separate manual save slot. My advice is to set a manual save at the start of each day and leave it alone, that way if you end up reaching the night overwhelmed, you can at least fall back and try and spend your scrap differently to better prepare yourself.

[h2] Is dying a big deal? Aren’t there roguelite elements? [/h2]

Yes and no. The game’s description mentions roguelite elements, but it’s not in the traditional sense of “when you die at the end of a run you get so many points or unlocks that make the next run easier”. When you die, you’re dead, and it’s up to you to figure out if you can go back to your save and salvage the situation or if you’ve just got to start over again from scratch.

There are gameplay changing upgrades you can find, but don’t go into this expecting a run-based roguelite.

One thing worth considering for the devs is offering multiple auto-saves so you can go back a couple days if needed.

[h2] So, player with way too many simulator games— [/h2]

YOU SHUT YOUR FILTHY MOUTH, THERE’S NO SUCH THING!

[h2] Okay…player with a lot of simulator games, is it a hit or a miss? [/h2]

Oh good gracious it’s a hit. I’m not joking when I say I could not wait for this game to drop. I’m playing through Dark Souls 3 for the first time, I’m halfway done playing it, I stopped playing to play this instead.

There are some rough edges to sand out, but the developer is active and open to feedback in a way that few devs are. I can’t tell you how many early access games, for example, I’ve seen the developer shut down everything the community says, and the point of EA is to build your game alongside your community.

The Spotter is a fully released title, they don’t have to listen to us if they don’t want to, but they’re active in the discussions and open to player feedback, and that’s to be praised.

Some things that need work (that the dev is already aware of and working on) are performance improvements for handhelds, UI size improvements, and I wouldn’t mind if the “no toilet humor” toggle fully removed it instead of just largely mitigating it (please, [i] please [/i], I play almost exclusively with headphones on XD), but none of the rough edges are enough to diminish the enjoyment of the game.

So, Spotter, grab a shovel and get to diggin’, the underground city isn’t gonna find itself.

review:
[h1] Fellows fans of "A Game About Digging A Hole" - we have found a worthy successor! [/h1]

I always love seeing new games come along that create entire new subgenres. That is what happened with A Game About Digging A Hole, and after quite some time, we have finally found a game that is worthy of taking a spot alongside the original as being one of the best in the "genre".

This game is very familiar to AGADAH in terms of gameplay loop, but provides a lot of additions that keep the game fresh, and innovative more than derivative.
Dig for resources? Sure! But don't forget all the collectibles. Or the base building, or the Tower-defense. Or the "landmarks" to find underground.
Simply put, The Spotter: Dig or Die is a well made and interesting successor to AGADAH in what has been a long line of titles that haven't quite hit that mark.
I am very excited to play more of this, and loved checking it out with my chat!

そしてリスタートはセーブした地点か、永続強化など一切無い状態ではじめから。
つまりプレイヤースキルと知識で来世に再チャレンジしていく昔ながらのスタイルなのだが……ただでさえ労力がかさむワリに虚無りやすい採掘ゲームジャンルで、裸一貫でまた放り出されるのは結構こたえるものがある。

そしてスタミナ制が良し悪し。ある程度掘ったら地上or地中のチェックポイントにある冷蔵庫で冷えたビールをキュッとやる必要があり、メリハリにはなっている。
が、ティアが進んで複雑かつ忙しい堀り生活になってくると、長～い穴を何度も何度も往復してのスタミナ回復に「おいまたかよ」「もう戻るのかよ」とだんだんイラッとしてくる。

あとたまに、ミュータントがまだ来ない昼間のうちから愛犬をさらいにUFOが来たりする。もちろんこれも迎撃の為に地上へ戻らないといけない。

総じてプレイヤーへ背負わせる遅延行動（またの名をゲームの延命という）が多すぎる為、ここらへんのバランス調整が行われるまではオススメできないかな。

このゲームに興味を持った方はトレーラーなどを見て「掘りながらミュータントをなんとかする忙しいゲーム」とあらかじめ察したうえで購入すると思われるが、
自分は「こんなに掘れるようになったな！」「拠点強くなっていったな！」と実感する段階へ至る前に、面白さよりも疲労が勝ってしまった。

ゲーム自体は9時間程度でクリアできました。
Intel Core UltraシリーズのCPUを使用している方は起動するとクラッシュする問題が発生しています。
回避策としてデバイスマネージャーからNeral processors(ニューラルプロセッサ)の項目を見つけてAI Boostを無効化すれば起動できます。
ドローンを使うと戻れないバグがあります、まだバグがかなりありそうなので安定するまでおススメできない状況です。
developer_response:
ご意見を共有していただき本当にありがとうございます。いただいたフィードバックは、ゲームの改善にとても役立っています。

この問題についてはすでに2回お知らせを出していますが、改めてご説明させてください。進行不能になる原因は、デモ版のセーブデータを製品版で読み込んでしまうことにあります。この影響でゲームの進行が壊れてしまいます。最新のパッチでは新規プレイヤーにはこの問題は発生しないよう修正されています。ただし、すでにプレイされた方のセーブデータをこちらで削除することはできません。そのため、新しくゲームを開始していただくことで進行不能の問題は解消されます。

Intel Core UltraシリーズのCPUに関する問題については、ゲーム側の問題ではなくUnreal Engineに関連するものです。現在、回避策はご案内しており、引き続き解決方法を探しながらUnreal Engineの開発元にも問い合わせを行っています。

私たちはプレイヤーの体験をとても大切にしており、安定性の向上と問題の修正に継続的に取り組んでいます。もしよろしければ、もう一度ゲームを試していただけると嬉しいです。そして体験が改善されたと感じていただけた場合は、レビューの更新をご検討いただけますと大変ありがたいです。

I played the demo of the game and was really amazed at what an addictive loop of digging for resources, finding interesting artifacts underground and then upgrading my gas station was. I was able to playtest the game and I have about 13 hours into it and I'm towards the very end. I ended up buying this game for a few friends since I did receive he product for free. I'm not friends with the devs, but do want this game to be successful because I believe that the devs will keep releasing more and more content for the game. 

I can say for a fact that for the 10 dollars they are asking for the game, is a steal. You basically need to upgrade your gas station to defend against zombies until you are able upgrade your receiver fully and dig deep enough to get the presidents message. To do this, you will be juggling stamina and your backpack limit as you dig deeper and deeper under the gas station to get resources to upgrade everything from your health to turrets. Under the gas station are interesting points of interests, bunkers and artifacts. 

The game is very contained and focused. I would def recommend this game based on the price, addicting gameplay loop and devs that are willing to listen to community feedback and I think will just continually add to this game.

[h1]为什么世界末日了还有外星人悄咪咪地开飞碟过来偷狗！[/h1]

《僵尸末世：地底全是财，挖宝造炮台》是一款游戏节奏比较紧张的挖矿塔防游戏，玩家将扮演一个在末世生存的挖矿塔防大师？在末世僵尸横行的地方采集物资搭建防御，同时通过积攒的物资尽快地把信号站修好向外界发出信号。

游戏的玩法比较简单，玩家只需要通过挖掘地底废料放进资源粉碎机里面进行资源置换，通过置换出来的三种基础资源来升级基地的防御能力和挖矿的各种功能就行了。

同时游戏在传统挖矿塔防的基础上增加了不少小彩蛋游戏，像是像素打僵尸射击游戏和地底溜杀人魔以及激光跑酷这些奇妙小游戏可以给部分大佬挑战一下自己的小游戏实力。

下面是攻略小贴士时间：
玩家可以通过让狗被外星人抓走然后再救回来获得一个能帮助玩家夜晚守家的超级狗子（别问狗子咋突然能召唤飞碟帮你守家了，就当狗子出门学习了先进的外星科技吧(´▽｀)ノ♪），外星人只会在前两级的信号范围内刷新，并且只刷新在白天，狗子学成归来以后外星人依旧还会来偷狗，如果在狗子被偷期间玩家把基地升到三本，那狗子就救不回来了(ಥ_ಥ)。

玩家在前期不要迷信游戏的新手教程，傻fufu地直接激活基地（手控炮塔也会被僵尸冲烂的（Ծ‸Ծ），一般推荐前期多挖两铲子攒够两个自动炮塔的资源再去激活基地或者是往基地正门那里直接往下挖到遗物选基地护罩（护罩挺好用的，而且升级基地防御的时候会满血刷新一次，对于前期舍不得花资源修基地的玩家来说还是挺重要的）

游戏的主炮塔有三个攻击分支选择，玩家可以选一个自己比较喜欢的攻击分支。（个人感觉大炮后期自动攻击有待加强，手控大炮还好，自动大炮因为大炮的无需装填和无需冷却的俩终极升级反而导致大炮自动守夜能力被大削了，还有大炮的攻击AI升级以后有时候到了白天也会不停地乱攻击，极其浪费火力。）

溜杀人魔小游戏跑不赢的可以等四本以后点慢慢回血再来挑战杀人魔（每次跑的时候记得按附近的按钮，可以更快地打开封锁的大门），激光跑酷这个加血没辙，容错太低了（没必要强求），打僵尸这个就是没有奖励的小游戏（喜欢打僵尸的可以试试。）

还有玩家在升满大本以后激活信号广播时记得不要千万不要急着跑核打击避难所，等电脑的核弹倒计时结束弹的避难所密码出来以后再跑核避难所（又是一个小细节(๑>؂<๑））

整体上来说本作的游戏性还算不错，就是游戏的上手难度略高，爽感偏慢热一点，适合喜欢玩有点挑战性的塔防挖矿爱好者入手。

review: Dig by day, slaughter mutants by night - what more could you ask for? Genuinely a fun game, cool backstory too! Good progression, starts slow, but soon your skills and tools ramp up and you can dig more efficiently. Looking forward to playing more!

I came in expecting a simple “dig stuff up, survive the night” loop, but it’s way more satisfying than that. The day/night structure works really well. Digging during the day trying to push deeper and deeper while balancing the time it takes to get back up to defend your base in time is actually pretty fun.

The mining, upgrading, base defense, and gear progression all feed into each other in a way that makes the loop easy to get hooked on. I also like that you’re not just placing defenses and watching, you are actively involved in the fights.

If you like mining, tower defense, base building, and games that let you steadily snowball into stronger builds, this is absolutely worth checking out. It has a cool identity and feels genuinely fun to play. Lots of cool funny secrets to discover as well.
